A. muciniphila alleviates IBS-D-associated intestinal inflammation and barrier dysfunction by modulating gut microbiota composition and inflammatory signaling pathways, supporting its potential as a microbiota-based therapeutic strategy for IBS-D.
authors: Ucar M, Celebi D, Celebi O, Baser S, Guler MC, Tanyeli A, Kılıclıoglu M, Yıldırım S.
screening_reason: Investigates how Akkermansia muciniphila modulates gut microbiota dysbiosis and intestinal inflammatory signaling in IBS-D.
summary_ja: 本研究では、ストレス誘発下痢型過敏性腸症候群（IBS-D）ラットモデルを用いて、Akkermansia muciniphilaの投与効果を検証した。IBS-Dモデルラットでは、腸内細菌叢の乱れ、腸管バリア機能の低下、およびTLR4/NF-κB/NLRP2経路の活性化に伴う炎症性サイトカインの上昇が認められた。A. muciniphilaを投与したところ、炎症反応および同シグナル伝達経路が抑制され、タイトジャンクション関連タンパク質の不全が改善した。さらに、Faecalibacterium prausnitziiなどの有用菌が増加し、腸内細菌叢の異常が一部是正された。
summary_en: This study investigated the therapeutic effects of Akkermansia muciniphila in a stress-induced rat model of diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D). Supplementation with A. muciniphila suppressed TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP2 inflammatory signaling and reduced serum cytokine levels. Additionally, it restored intestinal tight junction protein expression and partially corrected dysbiosis by increasing beneficial taxa such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii.
key_finding_ja: Akkermansia muciniphilaの投与は、TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP2シグナル経路の抑制と腸内細菌叢の是正を介して、IBS-Dモデルラットの腸管炎症とバリア機能障害を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 下痢型過敏性腸症候群に対する腸内細菌叢を標的とした新たなプロバイオティクス治療戦略の開発につながる可能性がある。

title: High dietary B 12 is associated with reduced gut microbial B 12 biosynthesis capacity and lower fecal short-chain fatty acids in healthy United States adults.
abstract: Vitamin B 12 is acquired through the consumption of animal-source foods and supplements. In animal models, interventions with B 12 and/or methionine influence fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) concentration. Yet the relevance of dietary B 12 to microbially produced SCFAs in humans is unknown. This study determined associations between dietary B 12 and the gut microbiome in a deeply phenotyped cohort of healthy U.S. adults. Habitual diet and fecal shotgun metagenomes were integrated alongside measurements of fecal SCFAs, plasma SCFAs, and plasma B 12 ( n = 277). Vitamin B 12 intake ranged from 2.4 to 1062 µg/day, and nearly all participants were B 12 replete. Stratification of participants into adequate (2.4-8.51 µg/day) and high B 12 intake (>8.51 µg/day) groups revealed the association of high intake with a reduction in bacteria capable of anaerobic B 12 biosynthesis. High B 12 intake was also associated with lower fecal SCFA concentrations even after controlling for fiber and methionine intake. Differences in microbial taxa between dietary groups were limited. However, machine learning models demonstrated the ability to predict fecal propionate and butyrate from microbial pathways in the adequate or no supplement groups, but not in the high intake or supplement groups. Our results indicate that dietary B 12 greater than 8.51 µg/day may be associated with reduced microbial synthesis of B 12 and lower fecal SCFA production.
authors: Hilliard MA, Oliver A, Wilson SMG, Shahab-Ferdows S, Hampel D, Bennett BJ, Allen LH, G Lemay D.
screening_reason: Directly examines how dietary vitamin B12 influences gut microbial B12 biosynthesis and short-chain fatty acid metabolic output.
summary_ja: 米国人健常者を対象とした本研究では、食事からのビタミンB12摂取量と腸内細菌叢および糞便中短鎖脂肪酸（SCFA）との関連を解析した。ビタミンB12を高用量（8.51 µg/日超）摂取する群では、嫌気性B12合成能を有する腸内細菌の減少が見られた。さらに食物繊維やメチオニン摂取量を調整した後も、高用量摂取群において糞便中のSCFA濃度が低いことが確認された。以上の結果は、高用量のビタミンB12摂取が腸内細菌によるB12合成能およびSCFA産生能の低下と関連している可能性を示唆している。
summary_en: This study analyzed associations between dietary vitamin B12 intake, the gut microbiome, and fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels in a cohort of healthy U.S. adults. High dietary B12 intake (>8.51 µg/day) was associated with a reduction in bacteria capable of anaerobic B12 biosynthesis. Furthermore, high B12 intake was correlated with lower fecal SCFA concentrations even after controlling for fiber and methionine intake.
key_finding_ja: 健常成人において、高用量のビタミンB12摂取は嫌気性B12合成能を持つ腸内細菌の減少および糞便中短鎖脂肪酸濃度の低下と関連していた。
why_it_matters_ja: 日常的なビタミンB12の高用量摂取が腸内細菌の代謝機能や短鎖脂肪酸産生に影響を与える可能性があり、サプリメント等による過剰摂取の評価において考慮されるべきである。

title: Intestinal flagellin drives multisystem inflammation through TLR5-IL-15-ARA axis.
abstract: Background Systemic inflammatory diseases including rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis (AS), IBD and long covid share convergent multi-organ phenotypes. Long covid provides a tractable model for dissecting gut-driven mechanisms of systemic inflammation, given its defined temporal onset and treatment-naïve postinfectious context. Objective To characterise a gut-driven mechanism of systemic inflammation in long covid and assess its cross-disease correlates in RA, AS and IBD. Design Comparative metagenomic analyses across RA, AS, IBD and long covid cohorts. Long covid was established as a paradigm for postdysbiotic inflammatory diseases, single-cell RNA sequencing and functional studies in longitudinal human cohorts and co-infection mouse models (SARS-CoV-2 and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ) were employed to dissect cellular and molecular mechanisms. Genetic and pharmacological interventions targeting the interleukin (IL)-15-arachidonic acid (ARA) axis were validated for therapeutic efficacy. Results Flagellated bacterial expansion defined a shared intestinal signature across all four diseases. Mechanistic studies in long covid demonstrated that flagellated bacteria activated toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5) on neutrophils, triggering the formation of neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) and IL-15 release. IL-15 subsequently stimulated macrophage ARA production. The co-infection murine model recapitulated multi-organ pathophysiology of long Covid, including pulmonary fibrosis and intestinal lymphoid aggregates. Genetic ablation of macrophage ARA synthesis or neutrophil IL-15 attenuated lung pathology, whereas gut microbiome clearance with gentamicin uniquely suppressed systemic inflammation. Conclusions We delineate a flagellin-TLR5-IL-15-ARA axis as a candidate mechanism driving systemic inflammation in long covid. These findings position intestinal flagellin as a candidate therapeutic target and ARA as a potential biomarker for long covid, warranting prospective validation across inflammatory disease boundaries.
authors: Geng J, Zhu Y, Chen S, Song X, Huang Q, Ma H, Liu H, Yang X, Zhang X, Zhang J, Luo L, Wu Y, Dai S, Cheng J, Zhang C, Chen L.
screening_reason: Demonstrates how intestinal flagellated bacteria trigger systemic inflammation via an intestinal host-microbe flagellin-TLR5 signaling axis.
summary_ja: 関節リウマチ、強直性脊椎炎、炎症性腸疾患、およびLong COVIDに共通する腸内細菌叢の特徴として、鞭毛細菌の増加が同定された。機構解析により、腸内の鞭毛細菌が好中球のTLR5を活性化してIL-15の放出およびNETs形成を誘導し、これがマクロファージによるアラキドン酸（ARA）産生を刺激することが明らかになった。感染マウスモデルにおいてマクロファージのARA合成や好中球のIL-15を遺伝的に欠損させると肺病変が軽減し、抗生剤による腸内細菌の除菌は全身性炎症を抑制した。本研究は、腸内フラジェリン-TLR5-IL-15-ARA軸が多臓器にわたる全身性炎症を駆動する機序である可能性を示している。
summary_en: Comparative metagenomic and functional analyses revealed that flagellated bacterial expansion is a shared intestinal feature across several inflammatory diseases, including long COVID. Intestinal flagellin was found to activate neutrophil TLR5 to induce IL-15 release, which subsequently stimulated macrophage arachidonic acid (ARA) production. Genetic or pharmacological targeting of this pathway or clearance of the gut microbiota attenuated systemic inflammation and pathology in mouse models.
key_finding_ja: 腸内の鞭毛細菌がTLR5-IL-15-アラキドン酸軸を介して好中球とマクロファージを活性化し、全身性の多臓器炎症を駆動するメカニズムが解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌由来のフラジェリンやアラキドン酸代謝経路が、Long COVIDをはじめとする全身性炎症性疾患の新たな治療標的やバイオマーカーとなる可能性が期待される。

title: A human pluripotent stem cell triculture platform to elucidate microglial regulation of retinal ganglion cells in neuroinflammation.
abstract: Optic neuropathies, including glaucoma, are characterized by the progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), ultimately leading to irreversible vision loss. Increasing evidence implicates microglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, as key modulators of RGC health and disease progression. However, the precise mechanisms by which microglia influence RGCs remain poorly understood, particularly in the human context. In this study, we established human pluripotent stem cell-derived coculture systems incorporating microglia, astrocytes, and RGCs to explore how microglia shape RGC growth and maturation under physiological conditions. We first examined the impact of homeostatic microglia on RGCs in both coculture and triculture systems, revealing distinct influences of cell types in coculture compared to when they were grown individually. We then modeled inflammatory states by activating microglia with lipopolysaccharide and evaluated their effects on RGCs both directly and in the context of astrocyte coculture. This stepwise, reductionist approach enabled us to dissect the cellular interactions driving RGC vulnerability in inflammatory conditions relevant to optic neuropathies. Our findings provide insight into the complex neuroimmune landscape that underlies RGC degeneration and identify key pathways that may serve as therapeutic targets across a range of optic nerve diseases.
authors: Harkin J, Gomes C, Afify R, Patil SV, Hetzer SM, Tutrow KD, Peña KH, Baker A, Lavekar SS, Huang KC, Meyer JS.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
screening_reason: The study directly investigates microglial regulation of retinal ganglion cell loss within a neuroimmune and neuroinflammatory cell culture framework.
summary_ja: ヒト多能性幹細胞から誘導したミクログリア、アストロサイト、網膜神経節細胞（RGC）を含む三次元/共培養プラットフォームを構築した。定常状態のミクログリアがRGCの成長と成熟に与える影響を解析し、細胞種間の複合的な相互作用を確認した。さらにLPS刺激により炎症状態のミクログリアを再現し、単独およびアストロサイト存在下でのRGC障害機序を段階的に解析した。このプラットフォームは視神経症における神経免疫応答とRGC脱落のメカニズム解明に寄与する。
summary_en: Researchers developed a human pluripotent stem cell-derived triculture system incorporating microglia, astrocytes, and retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) to model neuroinflammatory conditions. The study characterized the differential impacts of homeostatic versus LPS-activated microglia on RGC growth, maturation, and vulnerability both directly and via astrocyte crosstalk. This human cell model provides insights into neuroimmune cellular interactions underlying RGC degeneration in optic neuropathies.
key_finding_ja: ヒトiPS細胞由来のミクログリア、アストロサイト、網膜神経節細胞を用いた三次元共培養モデルを確立し、神経炎症下におけるミクログリアのRGC制御機構を明らかにした。
why_it_matters_ja: ヒト細胞に基づく本培養プラットフォームは、緑内障などの視神経疾患における神経免疫クロストークの理解や治療標的の探索に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Endocannabinoids and related lipids in host metabolism-gut microbiome signalling.
abstract: Over the past two decades, it has become clear that the two endocannabinoids, anandamide and 2-arachidonoyl-glycerol, are only the tip of an iceberg of a larger signalling system composed of hundreds of chemically similar fatty acid derivatives, including 2-monoacylglycerols, N-acylethanolamines and other N-acylamines. Unlike the endocannabinoids, these lipids only seldom bind the two cannabinoid receptors, of which CB1 is now recognized as a major player in both the central and peripheral control of energy metabolism. They modulate instead the activity of other G-protein-coupled receptors, as well as of ligand-activated ion channels and nuclear receptors, which also regulate energy intake, accumulation and expenditure. Bacteria inhabiting the gut as part of the intestinal microbiome also produce endocannabinoid-like molecules capable of activating host receptors in vitro. These discoveries led to current research into potential bi-directional communication between this 'extended endocannabinoid system', or endocannabinoidome, and the gut microbiome. Ongoing studies are investigating how this axis might control energy metabolism, particularly in response to diet.
authors: Silvestri C, Di Marzo V.
screening_reason: The article focuses directly on bidirectional signaling between the gut microbiome and host metabolism via endocannabinoids and related lipid signaling.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、エンドカンナビノイドおよびその類似脂質群（エンドカンナビノイドム）と腸内細菌叢との相互作用について論じている。これらの脂質メディエーターはカンナビノイド受容体やその他のGPCR、イオンチャネルなどを介してエネルギー代謝や摂食を調節する。腸内細菌もエンドカンナビノイド様分子を産生して宿主受容体を活性化することが分かっており、両者の双方向通信が注目されている。本稿では、食事応答やエネルギー代謝制御におけるこの拡大エンドカンナビノイドシステムと腸内細菌叢軸の役割を解説している。
summary_en: This review explores the bidirectional communication between the extended endocannabinoid system (endocannabinoidome) and the gut microbiome in regulating energy metabolism. In addition to classical endocannabinoids, numerous related lipid derivatives modulate host energy homeostasis through diverse receptors, while gut bacteria synthesize structurally similar lipids that activate these host pathways. The article highlights current insights into how this host-microbiome lipid signaling axis influences metabolic outcomes in response to diet.
key_finding_ja: 宿主のエンドカンナビノイドムと腸内細菌叢が産生する類似脂質との双方向シグナル伝達が、エネルギー代謝の制御に関与している。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事や腸内細菌叢に由来する脂質シグナルの解明が進むことで、代謝性疾患に対する新たな栄養的・薬学的介入アプローチの発見につながる可能性がある。

title: Emerging molecular mechanism of neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease: A JAK/STAT and TGFβ/SMAD signaling crosstalk.
abstract: Neuroinflammation has emerged as a convergent pathological signature of Parkinson's disease (PD), shaping both its onset and progression. Persistent activation of glial cells, driven by elevated proinflammatory cytokines, creates a self-reinforcing inflammatory milieu that accelerates dopaminergic neurodegeneration. Microglia, astrocytes, and Toll-like receptor (TLR)-mediated pathways converge to amplify this response, linking innate immune activation to chronic neurotoxicity. At the transcriptional level, the JAK/STAT signaling cascade governs cytokine-driven inflammation by promoting the expression of proinflammatory mediators, thereby sustaining immune activation. In contrast, the TGF-β/SMAD signaling functions as a critical counter-regulatory mechanism, maintaining immune quiescence and neural homeostasis through canonical SMAD-dependent signaling. However, in PD, this anti-inflammatory pathway becomes impaired, diminishing its neuroprotective influence. Emerging evidence suggests that hyperactivated JAK/STAT signaling can suppress TGF-β/SMAD activity, establishing a pathological dominance of proinflammatory signaling over neuroprotective restraint. This review synthesizes current understanding of the mechanistic interplay between these critical pathways, proposing that the imbalance between JAK/STAT activation and TGF-β/SMAD suppression represents a key candidate regulatory interface governing the neuroinflammatory trajectory of PD. Unraveling this crosstalk provides new insight into how signaling hierarchies shape glial phenotypes and neurodegeneration, while highlighting potential therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring immune equilibrium to mitigate PD progression.
authors: Purkayastha K, Roy A, Bhattacharya P, Borah A.
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
screening_reason: Focuses on the central role and molecular mechanisms of neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease, specifically JAK/STAT and TGF-beta/SMAD crosstalk in glial cells.
summary_ja: パーキンソン病（PD）における神経炎症の分子メカニズムとして、JAK/STAT経路とTGF-β/SMAD経路の相互作用に焦点を当てた総説である。PDでは、過剰に活性化したJAK/STATシグナルが免疫静穏化を維持するTGF-β/SMAD経路を抑制することで炎症応答が持続する。グリア細胞の持続的活性化と抗炎症機構の機能低下の均衡崩壊が、ドパミン作動性神経の脱落を促進する。これらのシグナル伝達のクロストークの解明は、PDの神経炎症を標的とした治療アプローチの基盤となる。
summary_en: This review highlights the molecular interplay between JAK/STAT and TGF-β/SMAD signaling cascades in driving chronic neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease (PD). Hyperactivation of proinflammatory JAK/STAT signaling suppresses neuroprotective TGF-β/SMAD pathways, establishing a persistent inflammatory milieu that accelerates dopaminergic neurodegeneration. Restoring the balance between these signaling hierarchies represents a potential therapeutic strategy to mitigate PD progression.
key_finding_ja: パーキンソン病では過剰なJAK/STATシグナルがTGF-β/SMAD抗炎症経路を抑制し、持続的な神経炎症とドパミン作動性神経脱落を引き起こすというメカニズムが提唱されている。
why_it_matters_ja: JAK/STATとTGF-β/SMADのシグナル均衡の回復を目指すアプローチが、パーキンソン病における神経炎症の進行を抑える新たな治療戦略となる可能性がある。

title: TAB2 Causes Neuronal Damage by Aggravating Microglia-Mediated Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Neuroinflammation plays a key role in exacerbating dopaminergic neuron loss in Parkinson's disease (PD). We identified TAB2 as an early-stage biomarker, which was elevated in PD patients' microglia. However, the role of TAB2 in the pathogenesis of PD remains unknown. In this study, we found that Tab2 knockdown inhibited the activation of microglia and protected neurons in PD models. STAT3, as a transcription factor for TAB2, regulated TAB2 expression. Mechanistically, TAB2 interacted with α-synuclein and facilitated the recognition of K63-linked ubiquitin chains, leading to the formation of the TAK1-TABs complex and activation of TAK1, which was ultimately followed by activation of the nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling pathway. Furthermore, microglia-specific knockdown of Tab2 significantly inhibited microglia activation, protected dopaminergic neurons, improved motor function, and attenuated anxiety-like behaviors in PD mouse model. We further showed that the FDA-approved drug, lumacaftor, suppressed microglial TAB2 expression and had potent anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects in PD models. Taken together, our study reveals that the STAT3-TAB2-NF-κB-IL-1β positive feedback axis in microglia is a crucial checkpoint that exacerbates neuroinflammation in PD. Therefore, these findings identify a pivotal role of TAB2 in regulating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation, suggesting that targeting TAB2 may be a possible therapeutic strategy for PD.
authors: Zhao Y, Huang Z, Gao J, Li A, Wang H, Chen Y, Zhu G, Zhang X, Jiang Y, Zhang M, Meng F, Zhang J, Du T.
screening_reason: The study directly investigates microglial-mediated neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease and defines the STAT3-TAB2-NF-kB signaling pathway.
summary_ja: パーキンソン病（PD）におけるドパミン作動性神経脱落の増悪因子として、ミクログリアを介した神経炎症が知られている。本研究では、PD患者のミクログリアで増加しているTAB2が、αシヌクレインとの相互作用やK63型ポリウビキチン鎖の認識促進を通じてTAK1-NF-κB経路を活性化することを示した。マウスPDモデルにおいてミクログリア特異的にTab2をノックダウンすると、ミクログリア活性化の抑制、ドパミン作動性神経の保護、運動機能障害および不安様行動の改善が認められた。さらに、既存薬のルマカフトルがTAB2発現を抑え、神経保護効果を発揮することが見出された。
summary_en: This study reveals that microglial TAB2 plays a critical role in Parkinson's disease (PD) pathogenesis by exacerbating neuroinflammation via the STAT3-TAB2-NF-κB-IL-1β signaling axis. Knockdown of Tab2 in microglia inhibited microglial activation, protected dopaminergic neurons, and improved motor and emotional deficits in PD mouse models. Additionally, the FDA-approved drug lumacaftor suppressed TAB2 expression and conferred neuroprotective effects.
key_finding_ja: TAB2がミクログリアにおけるNF-κB炎症経路を増幅してパーキンソン病の神経炎症と神経脱落を引き起こす重要因子であることを解明した。
why_it_matters_ja: TAB2を標的とした治療アプローチやルマカフトルのドラッグリポジショニングが、パーキンソン病の新しい神経保護療法に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids are associated with symptoms in chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome through the production of proinflammatory cytokines: Results from a comparative study.
abstract: In recent years we have witnessed increasing interest for the role of microbiota in the pathophysiology and management of prostatic diseases. However, there are several aspects to comprehend. Here, we aim to assess the gut microbiota composition and faecal microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids production (SCFAs) in the pathogenesis of CP/CPPS. All patients with CP/CPPS attending our urology centre, were enrolled in this study, and underwent urological examination, microbiological evaluation, intestinal microbiota analysis and measurement of interleukins in semen. A cohort of subjects who had undergone intestinal microbiota investigation for various reasons but did not exhibit any symptoms of urological disease, was used as control group. Laboratory data from the two groups were analysed in terms of gut microbiota composition and levels of SCFAs. We enrolled 37 patients and 45 controls. In the CP/CPPS patient group, the mean levels of interleukins were: IL-8 934 pg/ml, IL-10 64 pg/ml, IL-6 871 pg/ml. In this patient group, we found higher levels of Bifidobacteriaceae and Bacteroidaceae and lower levels of Prevotella and Lactobacillus with a Firmicutes/Bacteroides mean ratio at 0.27. The control group had a normal Firmicutes/Bacteroides mean ratio (1.6). The two groups showed a significant difference in total SCFAs levels ( p = 0.001) and in particular regarding indole-3-propionic acid ( p = 0.003) and butyric acid ( p p < 0.001). A difference in gut microbiota between patients with CP/CPPS and controls, together with a reduction in faecal levels of microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids and decreased IL-8 levels in semen, might be part of the pathophysiological mechanism in CP/CPPS.
authors: Cai T, Tamanini I, Odorizzi K, Ceccato T, Botti S, Gallelli L, Mazzoli S, Palmieri A, Bjerklund Johansen TE.
screening_reason: Evaluates gut microbiota composition and faecal microbial short-chain fatty acid production in chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome.
summary_ja: 本研究は、慢性前立腺炎/慢性骨盤痛症候群（CP/CPPS）患者37名と対照群45名を対象に、腸内細菌叢の組成および糞便中短鎖脂肪酸（SCFA）の関連を比較検討した。CP/CPPS群では対照群と比較してFirmicutes/Bacteroidetes比が著しく低下し、特定の細菌科・属の占有率に変化が見られた。また、CP/CPPS群において総SCFA量ならびにインドール-3-プロピオン酸や酪酸などの特定脂肪酸の減少が認められ、精液中IL-8濃度との相関も示された。提案された知見は、腸内細菌叢の変容とSCFAの低下がCP/CPPSの病態生理に関与している可能性を示唆している。
summary_en: This comparative study analyzed gut microbiota composition and fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) levels in 37 patients with chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) and 45 controls. CP/CPPS patients exhibited significant dysbiosis, characterized by an altered Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio and reduced levels of total SCFAs, including butyric acid and indole-3-propionic acid. These microbiological and metabolic alterations correlated with altered semen interleukin levels, suggesting a potential role in CP/CPPS pathophysiology.
key_finding_ja: CP/CPPS患者では対照群と比較して腸内細菌叢の構成変化とともに糞便中短鎖脂肪酸濃度の有意な低下が認められた。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸内細菌叢およびその代謝産物がCP/CPPSの発症機序に関与している可能性があり、新たな診断指標や治療アプローチにつながるか今後の検証が必要である。

title: Pyroptosis in Alzheimer's disease: Mechanisms and neuroinflammatory networks.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder pathologically characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau protein hyperphosphorylation, neuronal loss, and sustained neuroinflammation. In recent years, pyroptosis, a gasdermin-mediated form of inflammatory programmed cell death, has been recognized as a potential mechanism linking innate immune activation to neurodegenerative injury. This review summarizes the major molecular pathways of pyroptosis, including the canonical inflammasome-caspase-1-GSDMD pathway, the noncanonical caspase-4/5/11-GSDMD pathway, and alternative pathways involving caspase-3/GSDME and caspase-8, with a focus on their roles in the initiation, amplification, and propagation of neuroinflammation in AD. Current evidence suggests that AD-related stimuli, including Aβ aggregation, tau pathology, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and lysosomal damage, can induce inflammasome activation, gasdermin cleavage, and inflammatory mediator release, thereby sustaining chronic neuroinflammation. Concurrently, microglia, neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes may exhibit varying degrees of pyroptosis-related responses, contributing to impaired Aβ clearance, neuronal injury, glial dysfunction, and myelin pathology, respectively. This review further summarizes potential therapeutic strategies targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome, caspases, gasdermins, natural bioactive compounds, and the gut-brain axis. Overall, pyroptosis provides a novel framework for understanding the interplay between neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in AD; however, its cell-type-specific roles, stage-dependent effects, and translational potential remain to be fully elucidated.
authors: Wu X, Ye Q, Zi M, Jiang H, Meng S, Zheng J, Zeng S, Ma C, Hu X, Zhao B, Li H.
screening_reason: Review centered on pyroptosis pathways, gasdermin activation, and neuroinflammatory networks in Alzheimer's disease.
summary_ja: 本総説は、アルツハイマー病（AD）におけるパイロトーシスの分子メカニズムと神経炎症ネットワークの関与について整理しています。アミロイドβやタウの病理、ミトコンドリア障害、酸化ストレスなどのAD関連刺激がインフラマソームを活性化し、ガスカドミン切断や炎症性因子の放出を引き起こします。ミクログリアやニューロン、アストロサイト、オリゴデンドロサイトにおけるパイロトーシス関連反応が、Aβクリアランス障害や神経損傷、脱髄病理に寄与することが説明されています。さらに、NLRP3インフラマソームやカスパアーゼ、ガスカドミン、腸脳軸を標的とした治療可能性についても触れられています。
summary_en: This review summarizes the molecular pathways of pyroptosis and its involvement in neuroinflammatory networks in Alzheimer's disease. Pathological stimuli such as amyloid-beta, tau pathology, and oxidative stress induce inflammasome activation and gasdermin cleavage across various CNS cell types. The article also outlines potential therapeutic targets, including the NLRP3 inflammasome, caspases, gasdermins, and gut-brain axis pathways.
key_finding_ja: パイロトーシスはADにおける各種中枢神経細胞の障害や持続的な神経炎症の増幅に関与しており、病態進行を結ぶ新たなフレームワークを提供する。
why_it_matters_ja: ADにおける細胞種特異的かつ病期依存的なパイロトーシス制御の理解が、新たな治療アプローチの開発につながる可能性がある。

title: PARP inhibition attenuates neuroinflammation and demyelination in a rat model of multiple sclerosis: A longitudinal [ 11 C]PBR28 TSPO PET imaging study.
abstract: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) plays important role in DNA repair, but is also involved in other cellular processes. PARP inhibition was suggested to suppress inflammatory signaling and has been proposed as potential treatment for neuroinflammatory disorders like multiple sclerosis. Yet, its effects on lesion-associated neuroinflammation in vivo remain insufficiently understood. We therefore evaluated whether the PARP inhibitor PJ34 can attenuate neuroinflammation and demyelination, and whether treatment response can be monitored longitudinally, using positron emission tomography (PET) with [ 11 C]PBR28, a tracer for glial activation. In vitro, PJ34 was found to reduce [ 11 C]PBR28 uptake and ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (IBA1) immunoreactivity in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. In vivo, focal demyelination was induced in male Sprague-Dawley rats by unilateral lysolecithin injection into the corpus callosum and striatum, followed by PJ34 or vehicle treatment and serial [ 11 C]PBR28 PET imaging on days 3 and 7. PET revealed significantly lower tracer uptake in lesions of PJ34-treated animals compared to vehicle controls on day 3 (SUV mean 1.21 vs. 1.75; p 11 C]PBR28 PET imaging as a sensitive noninvasive biomarker of treatment response.
authors: Li G, Antunes IF, Ming Z, Wu C, Cornelissen B, de Vries EF.
journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
screening_reason: Evaluates PARP inhibition to attenuate neuroinflammation and demyelination in a multiple sclerosis animal model using longitudinal PET imaging.
summary_ja: 本研究は、多発性硬化症のラットモデルにおいてPARP阻害剤PJ34が神経炎症と脱髄を抑制するかをPETイメージングを用いて評価しました。In vitroにおいてPJ34はLPS刺激マクロファージの[11C]PBR28集積およびIBA1発現を低減させました。リゾレシチン誘発脱髄ラットモデルでは、PJ34投与により3日目のPET画像で病変部のトレーサー集積が有意に低下し、7日目にはIBA1陽性細胞の減少および脱髄の軽減が確認されました。
summary_en: This study evaluated whether the PARP inhibitor PJ34 attenuates neuroinflammation and demyelination in a rat model of multiple sclerosis using [11C]PBR28 PET imaging. In vitro, PJ34 reduced tracer uptake and IBA1 immunoreactivity in LPS-stimulated macrophages. In vivo, PJ34-treated rats exhibited significantly lower lesion tracer uptake on day 3, along with reduced microglial/macrophage activation and attenuated demyelination on day 7.
key_finding_ja: PARP阻害剤PJ34の投与により、ラット脱髄モデルにおけるミクログリア/マクロファージの活性化、病変部の[11C]PBR28集積、および脱髄が有意に抑制された。
why_it_matters_ja: PARP阻害が多発性硬化症の病変関連神経炎症を抑制する治療標的となり得るほか、[11C]PBR28 PETが治療反応の非侵襲的モニタリングに有用である可能性を示している。

title: Innate immunity-mediated inflammation and immunopathogenesis in HSV-1-infected encephalitis.
abstract: HSV-1 encephalitis (HSE) remains a devastating viral infection of the central nervous system despite effective antiviral therapy. Increasing evidence indicates that disease outcome is not determined by viral replication alone but by how innate immunity is calibrated within the brain. Studies of host susceptibility in childhood HSE have identified brain-intrinsic antiviral mechanisms, referring to central nervous system (CNS)-localized innate immune pathways that enable resident brain cells to sense and restrict HSV-1 infection, particularly TLR-dependent interferon responses, neuron-associated restriction factors, and other CNS-resident innate immune mechanisms. Host innate immune responses initially contribute to viral restriction, whereas excessive or unresolved activation can promote inflammatory amplification and long-term neurological injury. In parallel, HSV-1-mediated immune remodeling may weaken antiviral control and alter the subsequent inflammatory trajectory. Here, HSE is discussed as a dynamic immunopathological disorder in which protective innate immunity can transition into pathogenic neuroinflammation. Building upon these observations, we propose that host-directed therapeutic strategies should shift from uniform immune modulation toward stage-specific immune recalibration on the basis of viral control, antiviral competence, inflammatory persistence, and tissue repair.
authors: Yang S, Shen Y, Zheng C.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on central nervous system innate immunity, neuroinflammation, and immunopathogenesis during HSV-1 encephalitis.
summary_ja: 本論文は、単純ヘルペスウイルス1型（HSV-1）脳炎における自然免疫応答と病態形成のメカニズムに関する知見をまとめた総説です。中枢神経系における自然免疫経路は初期のウイルス制御に寄与する一方で、過剰または制御不能な活性化は炎症の増幅や長期的神経損傷を引き起こします。ウイルス複製だけでなく、脳内における自然免疫の調整状態が病勢を左右することが指摘されています。著者らは、一律の免疫修飾ではなく、感染や炎症の段階に応じた段階的な免疫再調整治療へのシフトを提唱しています。
summary_en: This review discusses the role of innate immunity and immunopathogenesis in HSV-1 encephalitis. While CNS-intrinsic innate immune responses initially restrict viral infection, excessive or unresolved activation can drive inflammatory amplification and neurological injury. The authors propose shifting host-directed therapeutic strategies toward stage-specific immune recalibration based on viral control and inflammatory persistence.
key_finding_ja: HSV-1脳炎において、脳固有の自然免疫は初期のウイルス抑制に不可欠であるものの、過剰な活性化は増幅された神経炎症と組織損傷を引き起こす。
why_it_matters_ja: HSV-1脳炎に対する治療戦略を単なる免疫抑制から病相に応じた段階的免疫調節へ転換するための概念的基盤となる可能性がある。

title: Impact of Infant Feeding Mode on Gut Microbiome Composition in Early Life: Evidence from an Egyptian Cohort.
abstract: The infant gut microbiome develops rapidly in early life, shaping immune maturation and metabolic pathways. Data from Middle Eastern populations remain limited. We studied Egyptian infants aged 1 to 6 months to assess feeding related differences in gut microbiome composition. Stool samples were collected and the gut microbiota was profiled using 16S rRNA gene sequencing targeting the V3-V4 region. Sequence processing, denoising, and taxonomic assignment were performed in QIIME2. Differentially abundant taxa between feeding groups were identified using LEfSe. Alpha and beta diversity, and co-occurrence networks were analyzed. Feeding mode was the dominant factor shaping microbiome composition and diversity. Artificial feeding showed Actinobacteria dominance, near absence of Bacteroidetes, and lowest diversity. Breastfeeding was associated with a more balanced phylum distribution, detectable Bacteroidetes, increased Proteobacteria, and significantly higher richness and diversity. Mixed feeding showed the highest alpha diversity and a Firmicutes dominated profile, consistent with a transitional microbial state. Beta diversity clearly separated breastfed from artificially fed infants, with mixed feeding intermediate. Genus level signatures differed by feeding mode. Artificial feeding enriched Bifidobacterium. Breastfeeding enriched facultative anaerobes including Escherichia Shigella and Enterobacter. Mixed feeding enriched fermentative genera such as Subdoligranulum and Eubacterium. Network analysis revealed structured co-variation among anaerobic commensals in breastfed infants and denser opportunistic connectivity in artificially fed infants. Feeding mode strongly influences gut microbiome development in Egyptian infants. Exclusive breastfeeding is associated with greater microbial richness and broader ecological structure, whereas formula feeding is linked to reduced diversity and a narrower community profile. Mixed feeding reflects an intermediate configuration. These findings support breastfeeding promotion for optimal early immune development.
authors: ELHindi S, Abdalla S, Azab MM, Bendary MM.
screening_reason: Investigates the composition, ecological structure, and diversity of the infant gut microbiome across different feeding modes.
summary_ja: エジプトの生後1〜6ヶ月の乳児を対象に、授乳方法が初期の腸内細菌叢形成に与える影響を16S rRNA遺伝子メタゲノム解析により評価しました。人工栄養はアクチノバクテリア門の優勢、多様性の低下、Bifidobacteriumの濃縮と関連していました。母乳栄養は多様性が高く、ProteobacteriaやEscherichia-Shigellaなどの通性嫌気性菌が多く見られました。混合栄養は最も高いα多様性を示し、中間的な菌叢構造を形成していることが明らかになりました。
summary_en: This study analyzed stool samples from Egyptian infants aged 1 to 6 months to evaluate how feeding modes affect early gut microbiome composition. Exclusive breastfeeding was associated with higher microbial richness and diversity, whereas formula feeding correlated with reduced diversity and Actinobacteria dominance. Mixed feeding resulted in the highest alpha diversity and represented an intermediate microbial configuration.
key_finding_ja: エジプトの乳児コホートにおいて、完全母乳栄養は高い微生物多様性と広範な生態学的構造を形成する一方、人工栄養は多様性の低下と特定の菌群への偏りをもたらすことが示されました。
why_it_matters_ja: 乳児期の適切な授乳選択が初期の腸内細菌叢形成や免疫発達を促す上で重要であることを示しています。

title: Dysphagia and gastrointestinal disorders in Parkinson's disease: towards a diagnostic standard operating procedure for the interprofessional neurological outpatient care team.
abstract: Gastrointestinal Disorders in people with Parkinson's disease (PwP) are able to cause widespread clinical symptoms which can be challenging to classify in day-to-day clinical practice. In the upper gastrointestinal tract (GIT) oropharyngeal dysphagia, esophageal motility disorders as well as delayed gastric emptying may cause nutrition problems and reduce the efficacy of oral pharmacotherapy. In the lower GIT, bacterial overgrowth and prolonged colorectal transit times induce different stages of constipation leading to reduced quality of life and GIT comorbidities as well. Most of these symptoms reflect alpha-synuclein pathology in both the enteric nervous system and at various sites of the peripheral and central nervous systems. Besides, the growing use of various device aided therapies may additionally raise specific clinical questions about the interference with the GIT motility. This standard operating procedure (SOP) is intended to provide specific recommendations for diagnostic steps as well as therapeutic options, especially for interprofessional neurological outpatient care teams.
authors: Claus I, Buhmann C, Fanciulli A, Klebe S, Marxreiter F, Süß P, Weise D, Warnecke T.
screening_reason: The paper directly addresses enteric nervous system alpha-synuclein pathology and gastrointestinal motility disorders in Parkinson's disease.
summary_ja: 本論文は、パーキンソン病患者における嚥下障害および消化管障害の病態と、外来診療チーム向けの標準作業手順書（SOP）について説明している。これらの消化器症状は、腸管神経系や中枢・末梢神経系におけるα-シヌクレイン病理を反映しているとされる。上部消化管の機能障害や下部消化管の小腸細菌過剰増殖・便秘などは、経口薬の有効性低下や生活の質の低下を引き起こす。多職種による神経外来チームが診断および治療選択肢を円滑に実施するための具体策が提示されている。
summary_en: This paper discusses gastrointestinal disorders and dysphagia in Parkinson's disease, which reflect underlying alpha-synuclein pathology in the enteric nervous system as well as peripheral and central nervous systems. Upper and lower gastrointestinal symptoms can cause nutritional deficits, reduce oral pharmacotherapy efficacy, and lower quality of life. The authors present a standard operating procedure to guide interprofessional outpatient teams through standardized diagnostic and therapeutic steps.
key_finding_ja: パーキンソン病における消化管障害は腸管神経系などのα-シヌクレイン病理を背景とし、その評価と治療のための多職種連携SOPが提唱された。
why_it_matters_ja: 腸管神経系の病理に基づく消化管症状を早期かつ系統的に評価・管理することは、パーキンソン病患者の薬物治療効果の維持やQOL向上につながる可能性がある。

title: Dynamic changes in the hindgut bacterial community of pre-weaning crossbred beef calves in a pasture-based system.
abstract: The early-life gut microbiome represents a window during which microbial alterations may impact long-term health and productivity. However, most research has focused on confined dairy systems with limited breed variation. To address this gap, we examined bacterial community dynamics in pasture-raised South Poll × Angus and Angus cow-calf pairs ( n = 7). Fecal samples were collected from calves at birth and weekly through 8 weeks, with dam's samples collected post-calving. DNA was extracted from fecal samples, and bacterial communities were profiled using the V1-V2 region of the 16S rRNA gene. Alpha diversity increased significantly with age (richness ρ ρ R ² = 0.33, ρ = 0.001; unweighted R ² = 0.38, ρ = 0.001), as calf communities converged toward adult reference states by 8 weeks. Sex exerted modest but detectable effects on community structure. Taxonomic analyses identified a core microbiome of 25 taxa that accounted for most community structure and defined discrete temporal phases of development. Early fecal samples were dominated by Lactobacillus , Bacteroides , and facultative anaerobes. These taxa declined rapidly with age, coincident with increases in Ruminococcus , Blautia , Dorea , Lachnospiraceae , and Clostridiales ( q Streptococcus , Dorea , and Bacillus and negatively correlated with Ruminococcaceae ( ρ > 0.3, q Lactobacillus . These findings establish foundational knowledge of microbiome assembly in a breed of beef calves growing in popularity and highlight microbial taxa and community structures that may relate to breed genetics influencing growth and health. Understanding microbial development in pasture-based beef systems provides an essential framework for designing microbiome-informed management or nutritional interventions aimed at improving productivity and sustainability, particularly in pasture-raised animals.
authors: Post A, Webb T, Indugu N, Smith BI, Pitta DW.
screening_reason: The research directly investigates gut microbiome assembly and bacterial community dynamics in beef calves.
summary_ja: 本研究は、放牧環境下で飼育された肉用子牛（サウスポール×アンガス交雑種およびアンガス種）の生後から8週齢までの腸内細菌叢の動態を分析したものである。アルファ多様性は加齢とともに有意に増加し、8週齢までに成牛の細菌叢構造へと近づくことが確認された。生後初期にはLactobacillusやBacteroidesなどの通気性嫌気性菌が優勢であったが、加齢に伴いRuminococcusやBlautiaなどの菌群へと迅速に変化した。
summary_en: This study evaluated the hindgut bacterial community dynamics in pasture-raised crossbred beef calves from birth through 8 weeks of age. Alpha diversity increased significantly with age, with calf microbial communities converging toward adult reference states by week 8. Early dominance of Lactobacillus and Bacteroides species rapidly shifted over time to higher abundances of taxa such as Ruminococcus and Blautia.
key_finding_ja: 放牧肉用子牛の腸内細菌叢のアルファ多様性は加齢とともに増加し、8週齢までに成牛の組成構造へと収束することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 放牧肉牛における初期の腸内細菌叢定着プロセスを解明することは、生産性や健康維持を目指した栄養・管理介入手法の開発に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Androgen signaling via sympathetic neurons regulates allergic pulmonary inflammation.
abstract: Sex differences in the rates of asthma onset and remission suggest that sex hormones may play an important role in the pathogenic mechanism underlying certain forms of asthma. Here, we demonstrate that increased endogenous androgen production in male mice can mitigate pulmonary type 2 inflammation after repeated allergen exposures during early life. Building on previous work showing that immune cells can respond to androgen signaling, we report that androgens also promote pulmonary sympathetic innervations, which can dampen type 2 inflammation via the neurotransmitter norepinephrine. Ablation of the androgen signal in sympathetic neurons is sufficient to disturb the establishment of sympathetic structures in the lungs of male mice, thereby amplifying type 2 inflammatory responses to allergens. Thus, an endocrine-neuroimmune axis contributes to the sexual dimorphism of allergic asthma during development.
authors: Tu X, Chen H, Ma X, Donovan C, Yang J.
screening_reason: The study investigates an endocrine-neuroimmune axis wherein sympathetic neurons modulate allergic pulmonary type 2 inflammation.
summary_ja: 本研究は、雄マウスにおいて高められた内因性アンドロゲンが気管支喘息モデルにおける2型気道炎症を軽減するメカニズムを解明した。アンドロゲン受容体シグナルは肺における交感神経の支配構造を促進し、ノルアドレナリンを介して2型炎症を抑制することが示された。交感神経細胞におけるアンドロゲンシグナルを欠損させると、肺の交感神経構造の形成が阻害され、アレルゲンに対する2型炎症反応が増強した。これらの知見は、内分泌・神経免疫軸がアレルギー性喘息の性差に関与していることを示している。
summary_en: This study demonstrates that endogenous androgen signaling in male mice reduces pulmonary type 2 inflammation after early-life allergen exposure. Androgens promote pulmonary sympathetic innervation, which suppresses type 2 inflammatory responses via norepinephrine release. Disruption of androgen signaling specifically in sympathetic neurons impairs pulmonary sympathetic network formation and exacerbates allergen-induced inflammation, establishing an endocrine-neuroimmune axis underlying asthma sexual dimorphism.
key_finding_ja: 交感神経細胞におけるアンドロゲンシグナルが肺交感神経網の形成を促進し、ノルアドレナリンを介して2型アレルギー性気道炎症を抑制することが解明された。
why_it_matters_ja: 発達期における性ホルモンと神経免疫系の相互作用の理解は、喘息の性差に応じた新たな治療法の確立に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Human gut microbiome as a composite health biomarker.
abstract: Using a cohort of 893 adults who underwent medical check-ups with rich data collection across diet, lifestyle, clinical labs, cardiac stress testing, and microbiome profiling, we show that a gut microbial health index (MHI), originally defined using a large meta-analysis of various human disease cohorts, is also substantially associated with lifestyle and diet. This association persists across the overall cohort, disease-free subsets, and individuals with common medical conditions such as hypertension and dyslipidemia. The gut MHI was positively correlated with factors such as variation in cardiac stress test fitness, fiber intake, and well-being, and negatively correlated with exposure to ultra-processed foods and markers of subclinical inflammation (WBC and CRP mostly within normal limits). Lipidomics profiling of a subcohort revealed that triglycerides correlate positively with ultraprocessed foods, and negatively with unsaturated fats, olive oil, and nuts, linking diet, MHI, and lipid profile. Estimating the contribution of modifiable dietary and lifestyle factors to the MHI uncovers actionable ways to improve or worsen the personal MHI. Analyses of previously published intervention studies showed that the MHI responds quickly to dietary changes, within the predicted range. Our findings emphasize the potential of using microbiomes, and specifically the MHI, as a reporter of overall health.
authors: Braun T, Harounian O, Hadar R, Ziv A, Ben-Avraham Shulman S, Kalter-Leibovici O, Efroni G, Ziv R, Fenesh M, Abbas-Egbariya H, Abramovich I, Amit S, Keller N, Truman K, Segev S, Amir A, Haberman Y.
screening_reason: The research focuses on assessing the human gut microbiome and gut microbial health index in relation to dietary, metabolic, and clinical parameters.
summary_ja: 893名の成人コホートを対象に、腸内細菌叢健康指数（MHI）と生活習慣、食事、体力、炎症マーカーの関連が解析されました。その結果、MHIは食物繊維摂取量や体力と正の相関を示し、超加工食品の摂取や潜在的炎症マーカーと負の相関を示しました。さらに介入研究の解析から、MHIは食事の変更に対して迅速に反応することが確認されました。これらの結果は、腸内細菌叢が全身の健康状態を反映する複合的なバイオマーカーとして有効であることを示しています。
summary_en: In a cohort of 893 adults, the gut microbial health index (MHI) was significantly associated with diet, lifestyle, physical fitness, and markers of subclinical inflammation. Lipidomics and intervention analyses showed that MHI correlates with dietary habits and responds rapidly to dietary modifications. These findings highlight the potential of using the gut microbiome and MHI as a composite reporter of overall health.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌叢健康指数（MHI）は食事や運動、炎症状態と密接に関連し、食事介入に対して迅速に変化することが示されました。
why_it_matters_ja: MHIが全身の健康や生活習慣を反映する有用な指標として、個人の健康評価や食事指導に応用できる可能性があります。

title: Gut-to-brain signaling: New frontiers in treating brain disorders.
abstract: Abstract The microbiota.gut.brain axis is essential for maintaining body balance. This review evaluates how altering this connection can treat various central nervous system disorders. First, we examine how the gut and brain communicate through neural pathways, immune responses, and chemical signals. We focus particularly on molecules produced by gut bacteria, such as short-chain fatty acids. These molecules are key regulators that maintain the blood.brain barrier and guide the development of microglia, the brain's primary immune cells. This review primarily discusses the bidirectional communication network between the gut and the brain via neural, immune, and chemical signals. This highlights the crucial role of gut bacterial metabolites in stabilizing the blood.brain barrier and guiding the development of brain immune cells. Additionally, we address significant challenges in this field, including establishing causal relationships, accounting for individual patient differences, and altering drug metabolism patterns. Additionally, we suggest that by targeting the gut outside the brain, we can move toward a new era of early, precise, and personalized holistic treatment for brain diseases.
authors: Pei H, Yao Y, Xu L, Bi J, Fan K, Fang Y, Lou H.
screening_reason: Focuses directly on the microbiota-gut-brain axis and the biological role of gut bacterial metabolites in guiding neuroimmune development and blood-brain barrier stability.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、中枢神経系疾患の治療に向けた腸脳相関および腸から脳へのシグナル伝達経路について概括しています。神経系、免疫系、化学的シグナルを介した双方向のコミュニケーションネットワークに焦点を当てています。特に、短鎖脂肪酸などの腸内細菌代謝物が血液脳関門の維持や脳の主要免疫細胞であるミクログリアの発達を誘導する役割を網羅しています。さらに、因果関係の証明や個人差、薬物代謝の影響といった課題と、腸を標的とした個別化治療の展望を提示しています。
summary_en: This review examines the microbiota-gut-brain axis and gut-to-brain signaling as therapeutic avenues for central nervous system disorders. It discusses how microbial metabolites like short-chain fatty acids regulate blood-brain barrier integrity and microglial development via neural, immune, and chemical pathways. The authors highlight current challenges, including establishing causality and accounting for individual differences, while proposing gut-targeted strategies for personalized treatment.
key_finding_ja: 腸内細菌が産生する短鎖脂肪酸などの代謝物が、神経・免疫・化学的経路を介して血液脳関門の維持やミクログリアの発達を制御していることが整理されました。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳疾患の早期予防や精密医療において、脳外の腸を標的とした新たな治療戦略の確立に貢献する可能性があります。

title: Effects of GLP-1 agonists on the gut microbiota in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review.
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a metabolic disease characterised by chronic hyperglycemia. The Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1 RAs) used in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) have been highlighted for their potential benefits to the gut microbiota in the context of this pathology. Therefore, it is important to investigate the relationship between microbiota and GLP-1 RAs used in T2DM. This review aimed at evaluating the effects of GLP-1 agonists on gut microbiota in T2DM individuals. The protocol was previously registered in PROSPERO, and the search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase databases in March 2025. Two reviewers have read the titles and abstracts and selected the included articles based on established criteria. The initial search identified 5532 publications, of which 17 studies were included: 12 preclinical and 5 clinical. Most were conducted in China between 2016 and 2025. GLP-1 agonists have been shown to modulate the gut microbiota, characterised by an increase in Bacteroidetes, Akkermansia muciniphila, and Lactobacillus. These changes are accompanied by an improvement of intestinal villi, increase in occludin expression, as well as an improvement in colonic inflammation. We identified a higher abundance of bacterial species associated with intestinal balance (eubiosis), accompanied by reduced inflammation and insulin resistance. Conversely, there was a lower abundance of bacteria related to dysbiosis, such as Firmicutes and Proteobacteria, which can be unfavourable when in excess. GLP-1 agonists influence the intestinal microbiota, improving metabolic parameters and anti-inflammatory effects. However, further clinical studies are needed to corroborate the findings of this review.
authors: Santos Dantas R, Souza Santos LV, Carvalho de Oliveira AG, Dos Santos Barreto M, Rego Rodrigues Silva DM, Macedo Moura PH, Dias Silva EE, Santana Santos R, Alves da Mota Santana L, Gandhi Gopalsamy R, Gibara Guimarães A, Pinto Borges L.
screening_reason: The systematic review focuses centrally on the modulation of gut microbiota composition by GLP-1 receptor agonists.
summary_ja: 本研究は、2型糖尿病におけるGLP-1受容体作動薬の腸内細菌叢への影響を評価した17件の論文（前臨床12件、臨床5件）に基づくシステマティックレビューである。GLP-1作動薬の投与により、Bacteroidetes、Akkermansia muciniphila、Lactobacillusなどの有用菌の増加が認められた。これらの変化は、腸絨毛の改善、オクルディン発現の上昇、大腸炎症やインスリン抵抗性の軽減と関連していた。一方で、FirmicutesやProteobacteriaなどのディスバイオーシス関連菌群の減少が確認された。
summary_en: This systematic review assessed 17 studies (12 preclinical and 5 clinical) to evaluate the impact of GLP-1 receptor agonists on the gut microbiota in type 2 diabetes. GLP-1 agonists modulated the gut microbiota by increasing beneficial taxa such as Bacteroidetes, Akkermansia muciniphila, and Lactobacillus while decreasing dysbiosis-related groups. These microbial shifts correlated with enhanced intestinal villi, increased occludin expression, and reductions in colonic inflammation and insulin resistance.
key_finding_ja: GLP-1受容体作動薬の投与は、Akkermansia muciniphilaなどの有用菌を増強し、腸内細菌叢のバリア機能向上および抗炎症作用を及ぼすことが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: GLP-1作動薬が腸内環境の調節を介して代謝改善や抗炎症効果をもたらす可能性が示されたことで、糖尿病治療の新たな機構理解に役立つ可能性がある。

title: Development of antibiotic-associated diarrhea in sepsis patients is associated with dysbiosis at baseline: Data from the PROGRESS Controlled Trial.
abstract: The randomized PROGRESS trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03333304) proved that early stop of antibiotics in sepsis guided by procalcitonin (PCT) changes leads, among others, to decrease of the incidence of antibiotic-associated diarrhea (AAD) and preservation of gut microbiome diversity. We aimed to explore an association of AAD with baseline microbiome composition. Patients with sepsis were followed-up for 28 days for AAD development. As PCT guidance led to decrease of AAD, only patients of the comparator arm, i.e. under treatment with standard-of-care (SoC) duration of antimicrobials, were considered for this exploratory analysis. In case of diarrhea, Clostridioides difficile infection was thoroughly investigated and excluded. Fecal samples were collected before initiation of antimicrobials and microbiome analysis was done by 16S rRNA Nanopore sequencing. Shannon diversity index was similar at baseline in 31 AAD (3.01; Q1-Q3, 2.49-3.49) and 54 non-AAD (2.83; Q1-Q3, 2.16-3.27; p: 0.456) patients. Relative abundance of Bacillota was lower (p: 0.038) and of Pseudomonadota higher (p: 0.019) in AAD patients. Abundance of the butyrate-producing anaerobic genus Faecalibacterium ≥ 0.15% was protective against AAD whereas abundance of Pseudomonas at baseline ≥ 0.75% (ORadj, 5.70; 95% CI, 1.70-19.06; p: 0.005) and Enterococcus at baseline ≥ 2.1% (ORadj, 7.16; 95% CI, 2.12-24.25; p: 0.002), were independent risk factors. Development of AAD in sepsis patients is associated with dysbiosis before start of antimicrobial treatment.
authors: Kyriazopoulou E, Stylianakis E, Damoraki G, Spyrou A, Symbardi S, Chrysos G, Adamis G, Giamarellos-Bourboulis EJ.
screening_reason: The trial directly examines baseline gut microbiome composition and dysbiosis as risk factors for antibiotic-associated diarrhea.
summary_ja: 本研究は、敗血症患者を対象としたPROGRESS臨床試験の標準治療群データを用いて、抗菌薬投与開始前の腸内細菌叢と抗生剤関連下痢症（AAD）発症との関連を評価した。解析の結果、ベースラインにおける細菌叢の全体的なShannon多様性指数には有意差がなかったものの、特定菌群の組成比に差が認められた。具体的には、酪酸産生菌であるFaecalibacterium属の相対存在量が一定以上であることがAADに対して保護的に働く一方、Pseudomonas属やEnterococcus属の存在比高値が独立したリスク因子として特定された。これらの知見は、抗菌薬治療開始前の腸内ディスバイオーシスがAAD発症に関与していることを示している。
summary_en: This exploratory analysis of the PROGRESS controlled trial investigated the relation between baseline gut microbiome composition and the onset of antibiotic-associated diarrhea (AAD) in sepsis patients receiving standard-of-care antimicrobial therapy. While baseline Shannon diversity did not differ significantly between AAD and non-AAD groups, specific microbial abundances correlated with risk. High relative abundance of Faecalibacterium was protective against AAD, whereas baseline elevations of Pseudomonas and Enterococcus were identified as independent risk factors.
key_finding_ja: 敗血症患者における抗菌薬投与前の腸内細菌叢の異常（ディスバイオーシス）が、抗生剤関連下痢症の発症リスクと関連していることが明かされた。
why_it_matters_ja: 抗菌薬投与開始前の腸内細菌叢プロファイリングは、敗血症患者における下痢発症リスクの予測や個別の予防的アプローチの選定に寄与する可能性がある。

title: A bioelectronic interface for continuous neuroinflammation monitoring and neuromodulation in Parkinson's disease model.
abstract: Neuroinflammation is increasingly recognized as a critical driver in the onset and progression of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet technologies capable of continuously tracking neuroinflammatory dynamics in vivo remain limited. Here, we report an implantable bioelectronic interface that integrates multiplexed aptamer based electrochemical biosensing with deep brain stimulation (DBS) for biomarker monitoring and neuromodulation in the rat brain. The biosensing platform introduces Tantalum@Au electrodes, engineered for chronic stability and biocompatibility, enabling simultaneous in vivo electrochemical monitoring of interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), α-synuclein (α-syn), and pH after DBS therapy. In freely moving PD rat models, the system maintained stable electrochemical performance for at least eight days post-implantation and captured dynamic biomarker fluctuations in response to targeted subthalamic nucleus DBS. DBS reduced IL-6 and TNF-α levels, indicating modulation of neuroinflammatory pathways, whereas α-syn level remained unchanged within the short-term window, consistent with the slower temporal dynamics of protein aggregation. DBS partially restored motor coordination though residual asymmetry persisted, paralleling clinical observations of symptom alleviation without complete functional recovery. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating continuous biochemical sensing with therapeutic neuromodulation to achieve a closed-loop platform, providing direct insight into molecular responses to DBS. This bioelectronic interface establishes a foundation for future biochemical-feedback-enabled neuromodulation strategies and precision therapeutic for neurodegenerative disorders.
authors: Zou S, Li J, Yu Y, Ou Y, Zhang Z, Liu G.
screening_reason: The study presents a bioelectronic interface directly designed for continuous in vivo monitoring of neuroinflammation dynamic markers in Parkinson's disease models.
summary_ja: パーキンソン病（PD）モデルラットにおいて、連続的な神経炎症モニタリングと視床下核への脳深部刺激（DBS）による神経変調を統合した埋め込み型バイオエレクトロニクスデバイスが開発された。本システムは自由行動下のラット脳内において、最長8日間にわたりIL-6、TNF-α、α-シヌクレイン、pHの動態を電化学的に同時計測することに成功した。DBSの実施により、神経炎症指標であるIL-6およびTNF-αの低下が確認され、運動協調性の部分的な回復が観察された。この技術は、リアルタイムな生化学的フィードバックに基づいたプレシジョン神経変調療法の実現に向けた基盤となる。
summary_en: Researchers developed an implantable bioelectronic interface combining multiplexed aptamer biosensing and deep brain stimulation (DBS) to track neuroinflammation dynamics in a Parkinson's disease rat model. The system continuously monitored IL-6, TNF-α, α-synuclein, and pH in freely moving rats for up to eight days. DBS reduced IL-6 and TNF-α levels and partially restored motor coordination, demonstrating the feasibility of a closed-loop platform for neuroinflammatory monitoring and therapeutic neuromodulation.
key_finding_ja: DBS治療中の脳内炎症性サイトカイン（IL-6、TNF-α）の動態を連続計測し、DBSが神経炎症を抑制して運動機能を一部回復させることを実証するバイオエレクトロニクス基盤を構築した。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経炎症のリアルタイムモニタリングと神経刺激を組み合わせた閉ループ医療技術の構築により、パーキンソン病などの神経変性疾患に対する精密な個別化治療の発展が期待される。

title: Loss of PHD3 rescues mice from Neuroinflammation and cognitive disorders induced by lipopolysaccharide or surgical trauma.
abstract: Objective Neuroinflammation is recognized as a contributing factor to cognitive disorders. Previous studies have demonstrated PHD3 drives microglia-mediated neuroinflammation. Present study aims to further clarify the role of PHD3 in both lipopolysaccharide (LPS)- and anesthesia/surgery (AS)-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive impairments. Methods Eight-week-old male wild-type and PHD3 knockout C57BL/6 J mice were used to establish LPS- and AS-induced neuroinflammation models. Cognitive function was evaluated using the Y-maze, open-field, and novel object recognition tests. Neuroinflammatory responses, microglial activation, synaptic proteins, and apoptosis-associated changes in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex were assessed by Western blotting and immunofluorescence staining. Furthermore, an adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated conditional microglial PHD3 knockdown model was established to investigate the role of microglial-specific PHD3 in neuroinflammatory regulation. Results PHD3 knockout significantly ameliorated LPS- and AS-induced cognitive deficits, accompanied by reduced expression of pro-inflammatory mediators TNF-α and IL-1β, and decreased the activation of NF-κB pathway in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex. PHD3 deficiency also attenuated microglial activation, restored postsynaptic density protein 95 (PSD95) and Synapsin I ‌(SYN1) levels, and reduced neuronal proapoptotic activation. Mechanistically, conditional microglial PHD3 knockdown recaptured the anti-inflammatory effects observed in PHD3 knockout mice via reducing LPS-induced inflammatory cytokines production, suppressing IKK/IκBα/NF-κB signaling activation, and modulating expressions of microglial activation-associated markers iNOS/CD86 and CD206/Arg-1. In addition, conditional microglial PHD3 knockdown attenuated LPS-induced upregulation of HIF-1α rather than HIF-2α expression. Conclusion Our results demonstrate that PHD3 deficiency exerts neuroprotective effects against systemic inflammation-induced cognitive dysfunction by suppressing microglial activation, synaptic damages, and neuronal apoptosis may through NF-κB signaling. These findings suggest that PHD3 may represent a promising therapeutic target for inflammation-associated cognitive disorders.
authors: Che J, Deng Y, Zhang X, Shi C, He Z, Dong J, Zhang J.
screening_reason: Studies the mechanistic role of microglial PHD3 in driving neuroinflammation and microglial activation in cognitive impairment models.
summary_ja: 本研究は、全身性炎症（LPS）や麻酔・手術侵襲（AS）による神経炎症および認知機能障害におけるPHD3の役割をマウスモデルで検証しました。PHD3欠損マウスでは、ヒポカンパスや前頭前皮質におけるミクログリアの活性化、炎症性サイトカイン発現、NF-κB経路の活性化が抑えられ、認知機能の低下が改善しました。さらにミクログリア特異的なPHD3ノックダウンでも同様の抗炎症・神経保護効果が再現されました。これにより、PHD3がミクログリア介在性の神経炎症を駆動するメカニズムの一端が解明されました。
summary_en: This study evaluated the role of PHD3 in systemic inflammation- and surgical trauma-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment using mouse models. PHD3 knockout and microglial-specific conditional knockdown attenuated microglial activation, inflammatory cytokine production, and NF-κB signaling while restoring synaptic marker levels and reversing cognitive deficits. These findings demonstrate that targeting microglial PHD3 reduces neuroinflammatory responses and neuronal apoptosis.
key_finding_ja: PHD3の欠損およびミクログリア特異的ノックダウンは、NF-κBシグナルの抑制を通じて全身炎症や手術侵襲によるミクログリア活性化と認知機能障害を著しく改善させました。
why_it_matters_ja: 神経炎症に関連する認知障害に対する新たな治療標的としてPHD3が有効である可能性が示唆されます。

title: Gut microbiome signatures during acute infection are associated with long COVID.
abstract: Background Long COVID (LC) manifests in 10%-30% of non-hospitalized individuals post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, leading to significant morbidity. The predictive role of gut microbiome composition during acute infection in the development of LC is not well understood, partly because of the heterogeneous nature of the disease. Objectives To determine whether the gut microbiome composition in the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection predicts subsequent LC and to investigate the role of microbiome signatures in disease subphenotypes. Design We conducted a longitudinal cohort study involving 799 outpatient participants tested for SARS-CoV-2 due to similar symptom presentation, including 380 SARS-CoV-2 positive and 419 negative individuals. Stool samples were collected at two time points for metagenomic sequencing. Logistic regression with L1 regularization was employed to predict LC based on the microbiome and clinical metadata. Results The individuals who developed LC harbored a distinct gut microbiome during acute infection compared to those who recovered fully and uninfected controls with similar symptomatology. However, the temporal changes in the gut microbiome between the acute (0-1 month) and post-acute (1-2 months) phases were similar across the three cohorts. Using machine learning, we showed that the gut microbiome carried a modest signal for subsequent LC, but model performance was insufficient for clinical prediction, likely reflecting the heterogeneous nature of LC. Finally, we identified four LC symptom clusters, with gastrointestinal and fatigue-only groups strongly linked to gut microbiome alterations. Conclusion The gut microbiome can potentially offer solutions for understanding the heterogeneous nature of LC. Larger cohorts and phenotype-aware computational algorithms may help overcome current model performance limitations and support the development of targeted diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
authors: Comba IY, Mars RAT, Yang L, Dumais M, Chen J, Van Gorp TM, Harrington JJ, Sinnwell JP, Johnson S, Holland LA, Khan AK, Lim ES, Aakre C, Athreya AP, Gerber GK, O'Horo JC, Lazaridis KN, Kashyap PC.
screening_reason: Investigates acute-phase gut microbiome profiles and metagenomic signatures associated with the development of Long COVID.
summary_ja: SARS-CoV-2感染後の罹患症状（Long COVID）の発症における急性期腸内細菌叢の役割を調べるため、外来患者799名を対象に縦断的コホート研究が実施されました。Long COVIDを発症した群では、急性期において全快群や非感染対照群とは異なる腸内細菌叢の構造が観察されました。機械学習を用いた予測モデルではLong COVIDの予兆に関して一定のシグナルが得られたものの、病態の多様性により臨床的な予測精度には達しませんでした。また、症状クラスタの解析から、消化器症状や倦怠感主体の群において腸内細菌叢の変動との強い関連が示されました。
summary_en: This longitudinal cohort study evaluated the predictive role of acute-phase gut microbiome composition in the development of long COVID among 799 outpatients. Individuals who developed long COVID exhibited distinct gut microbiome profiles during acute infection compared to fully recovered and uninfected controls. Machine learning models detected modest predictive signals, though clinical prediction accuracy was limited by disease heterogeneity. Notably, gastrointestinal and fatigue-only symptom clusters showed strong associations with specific gut microbiome alterations.
key_finding_ja: 急性期のSARS-CoV-2感染患者において、Long COVIDを発症する群は全快群や対照群と異なる腸内細菌叢の特徴を示し、特に消化器症状や倦怠感主体のクラスタで強い関連が認められました。
why_it_matters_ja: Long COVIDの病態解明や症状クラスタに応じた診断・治療戦略の構築に腸内細菌叢が活用できる可能性を示唆しています。

title: Global analysis of infant gut microbiota revealed distinctive maturation dynamics across lifestyles.
abstract: The infant gut microbiome develops during the first years of life and influences long-term health through its interaction with immune system development. However, our understanding of early-life microbiome assembly is biased by the predominance of infants with industrialized lifestyles from North America and Europe. Here, we address this bias by assembling a globally representative dataset of 14,979 infant gut microbiomes from 2746 individuals to train a microbiome maturation model that can characterize lifestyle-specific patterns of microbial maturation as a function of age. Models trained exclusively on industrialized infants perform poorly when applied to non-industrialized datasets. In contrast, more diverse models, including individuals from both lifestyles, achieve increased correlation between microbial and chronological age (ΔR 2 = 0.123). We identified differences in relevant taxa associated with the maturation in the different lifestyles. Additionally, our modeling approach detects a delay in the microbial maturation of independent cohorts of severely malnourished and preterm infants compared to healthy ones. Our results underscore the relevance of global diversity in microbiome research and provide deeper insights into context-dependent maturation dynamics of the infant gut microbiome.
authors: Bücking R, Pasquali G, Löber U, Buss C, Viemann D, Jarquín-Díaz VH, Forslund-Startceva SK.
screening_reason: Analyzes global infant gut microbiota maturation dynamics and assembly across different lifestyles and health conditions.
summary_ja: 本研究は、多様な地域から集めた2,746名の乳幼児（計14,979件の腸内細菌叢データ）を用いて、ライフスタイルに応じた腸内細菌叢の成熟モデルを構築したものである。産業化社会の乳幼児データのみで学習したモデルは非産業化社会のデータへの適用性が低いが、双方を含む包括的モデルにより細菌叢年齢と実年齢の相関が向上した（ΔR² = 0.123）。また、このモデルを用いて重度栄養障害児や早産児における細菌叢の成熟遅延を検出することに成功した。
summary_en: Using a globally representative dataset of 14,979 gut microbiomes from 2,746 infants, this study constructed a maturation model to characterize lifestyle-specific patterns of microbial assembly with age. Models trained only on industrialized populations performed poorly on non-industrialized datasets, whereas globally representative models improved the accuracy of microbial age predictions. Furthermore, the global modeling approach identified significant delays in microbial maturation among malnourished and preterm infants.
key_finding_ja: 世界的な多様性を反映させた腸内細菌叢成熟モデルの構築により、ライフスタイルごとの発達動態の差や栄養失調児・早産児における細菌叢成熟の遅延が実証された。
why_it_matters_ja: 地域や環境に応じた腸内細菌叢の標準的発達指標を確立することは、世界規模での小児の発育不全の早期発見や栄養介入効果の正確な評価に貢献する可能性がある。

title: EXPRESS: Spleen-mediated inflammation in ischemic stroke: mechanisms and targeted therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Emerging evidence from animal studies and clinical observations suggests that peripheral immune responses amplify neuroinflammation after acute ischemic stroke. This review briefly summarizes the interactions between peripheral immune responses and the ischemic brain, with a focus on the brain-spleen axis. Specifically, we dissect the mechanisms underlying spleen-mediated immune effects on the ischemic brain. We then critically summarize current spleen-targeted therapeutic strategies, ranging from physical and pharmacological interventions to stem cell-based approaches that reprogram splenic immune landscapes. Collectively, these insights aim to inform future immunomodulatory strategies targeting the brain-spleen axis.
authors: Wu S, Luo LH, Gao Y, Nan G.
journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
screening_reason: The review centrally addresses peripheral immune-brain interactions and spleen-mediated neuroinflammation following acute ischemic stroke.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、虚血性脳卒中急性期後における脳と脾臓の相互作用軸（脳-脾臓軸）に焦点を当て、末梢免疫応答が脳内神経炎症を増幅するメカニズムを概括している。特に、脾臓が媒介する免疫効果と脳虚血病態への関与について整理している。さらに、物理的・薬理的介入や幹細胞を用いた脾臓の免疫環境再プログラミングなど、脾臓を標的とした最新の治療戦略を批判的にまとめている。これらの知見は、脳虚血に対する新たな免疫調節療法の開発に寄与することを目的としている。
summary_en: This review outlines the communication along the brain-spleen axis following acute ischemic stroke, emphasizing how peripheral immune responses driven by the spleen amplify central neuroinflammation. The authors detail the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms of spleen-mediated post-stroke immune responses. Additionally, they evaluate emerging spleen-targeted therapeutic strategies, including physical, pharmacological, and stem cell-based interventions aimed at reprogramming the splenic immune landscape.
key_finding_ja: 虚血性脳卒中後において、脾臓を中心とする末梢免疫応答が脳の神経炎症を増幅させるメカニズムと、その治療標的としての可能性が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 脳-脾臓軸を介した末梢免疫制御システムへの介入は、脳卒中後の神経炎症軽減および脳損傷抑制のための新たな治療概念を提供する可能性がある。

title: Berberine and lactulose combination therapy attenuates neuroinflammation and hepatic injury in thioacetamide-induced hepatic encephalopathy in rats.
abstract: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) represents a severe neuropsychiatric manifestation secondary to advanced hepatic dysfunction, predominantly driven by hyperammonaemia and associated neuroinflammatory processes. Although lactulose remains a mainstay in the clinical management of HE due to its ammonia-lowering properties, its limited efficacy in attenuating neuroinflammation necessitates the use of adjunctive therapeutic strategies. Previously, we identified berberine, a plant-derived isoquinoline alkaloid, as an anti-HE agent via the reduction of neuroinflammation and NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Therefore, in the present study, we investigated the potential beneficial effects of co-administering berberine and lactulose in a rat model of thioacetamide (TAA)-induced hepatic encephalopathy. HE was induced via intraperitoneal injections of TAA (200 mg/kg) on alternate days for one week. Animals received oral pre-treatment with lactulose (8 mL/kg) alone or in combination with berberine (100 mg/kg) for 14 consecutive days. Comprehensive behavioural assessments were conducted alongside biochemical quantification of systemic ammonia, hepatic transaminases (ALT, AST), and oxidative stress markers (MDA, GSH) in both hepatic and cerebral tissues. Histopathological evaluations of the liver and brain further corroborated the biochemical findings. Notably, combination therapy significantly ameliorated cognitive deficits, reduced systemic ammonia burden, normalised liver and brain enzyme profiles, and markedly attenuated central neuroinflammatory signalling, as evidenced by reduced hippocampal NF-κB activation and GFAP immunoreactivity, in addition to suppressing hepatic NF-κB expression, surpassing the effects observed with monotherapy. Histological analyses revealed reduced neuronal degeneration and hepatic architectural disruption. These findings underscore the therapeutic potential of berberine-lactulose co-treatment in mitigating both hepatic and neuroinflammatory pathologies associated with HE, offering a promising adjunctive strategy for improving neurocognitive outcomes in liver failure.
authors: Saini A, Yadav SS, Ali SA, Datusalia AK.
screening_reason: The study directly tests a combination therapy aimed at reducing neuroinflammation and central inflammatory signaling in hepatic encephalopathy.
summary_ja: 本研究は、チオアセトアミド誘発肝性脳症ラットモデルを用いて、ベルベリンとラクツロースの併用療法の効果を検証した。併用投与により、単独投与と比較して全身の血中アンモニア濃度の低下や肝・脳機能の改善、認知機能障害の軽減が有意に認められた。さらに、海馬におけるNF-κB活性化やGFAP免疫応答の低下を含む中枢性神経炎症シグナルの抑制、ならびに肝臓の組織損傷緩和が確認された。これらの知見は、本併用療法が肝不全に伴う神経認知機能低下の改善に有用であることを示唆している。
summary_en: This study evaluated the combined administration of berberine and lactulose in a rat model of thioacetamide-induced hepatic encephalopathy. The combination treatment superiorly reduced systemic ammonia levels, normalized liver and brain enzymes, and attenuated cognitive deficits compared to monotherapies. Furthermore, it significantly suppressed central neuroinflammatory signaling, marked by decreased hippocampal NF-κB activation and GFAP immunoreactivity, alongside reduced hepatic inflammation and tissue damage.
key_finding_ja: ベルベリンとラクツロースの併用投与は、単独投与よりも強力に肝性脳症モデルラットの全身性アンモニア負荷、肝損傷、および海馬での神経炎症を緩和した。
why_it_matters_ja: 既存治療薬へのベルベリン併用は、肝不全に伴う神経認知障害および神経炎症を軽減する新たな補助療法となる可能性がある。

title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and functional alterations in Campylobacter -associated gastroenteritis using metagenomic approaches.
abstract: Campylobacter species are a major cause of bacterial gastroenteritis worldwide. Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from PCR-confirmed Campylobacter -positive patients and symptomatic PCR-negative controls, we reveal dysbiosis marked by reduced species richness (median Shannon diversity was significantly lower in the Campylobacter -positive group [3.24] vs. Campylobacter -negative group [3.63], P = 0.038), taxonomic shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa ( Campylobacteriaceae , Enterobacteriaceae , Pasteurellaceae ), and depletion of key commensals involved in short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production ( Ruminococcaceae , Bacteroidaceae , Eubacteriaceae ). These changes define a distinct microbial signature of infection, suggestive of a perturbed gut environment with reduced colonization resistance and impaired barrier function. Despite these taxonomic and ecological disruptions, resistome profiling showed no increase in the burden or diversity of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), suggesting that the observed microbiome disruption may not lead to broader expansion of ARGs in the gut microbiome. Whole-genome sequencing of cultured Campylobacter jejuni and C. coli isolates revealed common ARGs, including bla OXA-193 , tet (O), and gyr A_T86I, some of which overlapped with metagenomic findings. Moreover, metagenomics identified low-abundance Campylobacter species in PCR-negative controls, underscoring the need for greater taxonomic resolution. These results delineate a Campylobacter -associated microbial and functional footprint in the human gut, with implications for diagnostics and antimicrobial stewardship.
authors: Djeghout B, Ponsero AJ, Pedroso N, Savva GM, Elumogo N, Janecko N.
screening_reason: Metagenomic study focused on human gut microbiome dysbiosis, taxonomic shifts, and functional SCFA depletion during Campylobacter gastroenteritis.
summary_ja: カンピロバクター感染性腸炎患者とPCR陰性対照群の便検体を対象にショットガンメタゲノム解析を行った研究である。感染患者群では腸内細菌の種豊かな多様性が有意に低下し（Shannon指数 3.24対3.63、P = 0.038）、短鎖脂肪酸産生菌の減少と炎症関連菌の増加が確認された。一方で、薬剤耐性遺伝子（ARG）の全般的な蓄積や多様化はみられず、PCR陰性群の一部からも微量のカンピロバクター属菌が検出された。
summary_en: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing revealed that Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis is marked by reduced gut microbial richness and depletion of short-chain fatty acid producers without an increase in antimicrobial resistance genes. The study also detected low-abundance Campylobacter species in some PCR-negative controls.
key_finding_ja: カンピロバクター感染症に伴い菌種多様性の低下と短鎖脂肪酸産生菌の減少が生じるが、全体の薬剤耐性遺伝子量の増加は認められなかった。
why_it_matters_ja: カンピロバクター感染時の腸内生態系および薬剤耐性遺伝子の動態を詳細に把握することで、正確な診断や適切な抗菌薬使用管理に貢献する可能性がある。

title: Exploring the Early-Life Microbiomes of Preterm Infants and Their Childhood Health Outcomes (The BLOOM Study): Protocol for a Prospective, Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Establishment of the gut microbiome during the first years of life is critically important for long-term health and development. In preterm infants, microbial colonization is disrupted due to their developmental immaturity and the myriad of pre- and postnatal exposures. Unfortunately, this places them at an elevated risk for adverse health outcomes into childhood (eg, asthma and impaired neurodevelopment). Understanding the developmental trajectory of the microbiome in preterm infants, the factors predicting these microbial patterns, and the links to childhood health can offer opportunities to develop interventions and optimize health. Objective BLOOM (Begin a Life of Health With Observation and Optimization of the Microbiome) is a prospective, observational cohort study that aims to examine how early-life microbiomes shape the health and development of preterm infants into childhood (eg, asthma and neurodevelopment). Methods Infants ( Results Study recruitment and data/sample collection for BLOOM commenced in 2019; as of May 2026, we have enrolled 245 participants, and recruitment is ongoing. An initial characterization of early-life microbiome profiles for the first 105 infants enrolled in BLOOM was published online in December 2025. Conclusions BLOOM is a large, comprehensive prospective cohort study and biobank aimed at measuring the microbiome development of preterm-born children. This cohort will address significant research priorities through characterizing the patterns of microbiome development in preterm infants over the first 3 years postnatally and correlating these with health outcomes (eg, immune development, asthma and allergy risks, and neurodevelopment). It is anticipated that the results can be leveraged to identify factors and altered microbiome patterns underlying disease risk, design intervention strategies (eg, microbial therapeutics) for later clinical testing, and generate novel hypotheses of possible underlying mechanisms linking microbiome development to health.
authors: Asbury MR, Guedez A, Lee J, Mercer EM, Kasaba F, Rangipour Z, Kellner JD, Lacaze-Masmonteil T, Samara J, Leijser LM, Lebel C, Zein H, Hendson L, Murguía Favela L, McNagny K, Giesbrecht GF, Sycuro L, Alshaikh B, Arrieta MC.
screening_reason: Presents a prospective cohort study protocol specifically aimed at characterizing early-life gut microbiome development in preterm infants and its connection to childhood health outcomes.
summary_ja: 本論文は、早産児における初期腸内細菌叢の発達と小児期の健康（喘息や神経発達など）との関連を調べる前向き観察コホート研究「BLOOM研究」のプロトコルを示したものである。早産児では発生学的未熟さや種々の曝露により細菌叢定着が障害され、将来的な健康リスクが高まることが懸念されている。本研究では生後3年間にわたり縦断的に検体・データを収集し、マイクロバイオームの発達軌跡を追跡する。得られた成果から、将来的な予防的介入や個別化医療の基盤となるメカニズムの解明を目指している。
summary_en: This article details the protocol for the BLOOM study, a prospective observational cohort designed to evaluate how early-life microbiome assembly in preterm infants influences childhood health outcomes such as asthma and neurodevelopment. The study tracks preterm infants over their first three years postnatally with longitudinal biological sampling and health assessments. The resulting biobank and data aim to uncover underlying mechanisms and identify targets for novel therapeutic interventions.
key_finding_ja: 早産児の生後3年間における腸内細菌叢の発達軌跡と小児期の喘息や神経発達などの健康アウカムとの関係を縦断的に解明するBLOOM研究の計画が提示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 早産児特有の腸内細菌叢形成過程と疾病リスクとの関係を明らかにすることで、将来的な菌叢ターゲット治療や予防戦略の構築に資する可能性がある。

title: Amino acid metabolic reprogramming by gut microbiota: a novel metabolic checkpoint in the tumor microenvironment.
abstract: The gut microbiota plays a crucial role in human health, significantly influencing various physiological functions such as amino acid metabolism, which is essential for maintaining homeostasis and preventing disease. Recent progress in gut microbiota research has highlighted the intricate relationships between gut microbial communities and host amino acid metabolism, particularly in the context of cancer. This review focuses on consolidating the latest advances regarding how gut microbiota-mediated amino acid metabolism contributes to cancer development and progression. While dysbiosis has been implicated in various diseases, such as metabolic disorders, autoimmune conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, this review specifically examines the evidence linking gut microbiota and amino acid metabolism to cancer. Current studies suggest that alterations in gut microbial composition can lead to imbalances in amino acid availability and metabolism, thereby influencing systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and immune responses that may promote tumorigenesis. Despite these insights, significant challenges remain, including identifying specific microbial strains, deciphering their metabolic pathways, and understanding their complex interactions with host factors in cancer progression. This review aims to summarize recent preclinical and clinical investigations elucidating the mechanisms linking the gut microbiota, amino acid metabolism, and cancer, and to evaluate potential therapeutic strategies targeting the gut microbiome to modulate amino acid metabolism and improve cancer treatment outcomes. By highlighting the gut microbiota as a promising target for innovative oncological therapies, this review provides insights into microbiome-based interventions targeting amino acid-related pathways in cancer.
authors: Lin H, Deng X, Yang Y, Zhang R, Wang YD, Chen WD.
screening_reason: The paper directly reviews the central role of gut microbiota and microbial amino acid metabolism in modulating the tumor microenvironment.
summary_ja: 本総説は、腸内細菌叢によるアミノ酸代謝の調節ががんの発生および進行に与える影響に関する最新の研究知見をまとめて議論している。腸内細菌の組成変化に伴うアミノ酸利用性の破綻が、全身性の炎症や酸化ストレス、免疫応答を介して腫瘍形成を促進する可能性が示されている。また、特定の菌株の同定や代謝経路の解明、宿主因子との相互作用に関する課題についても整理している。アミノ酸代謝経路を標的とした腸内細菌叢への介入が、新たな癌治療法として期待されている。
