screening_reason: Investigates the neuropeptide phoenixin-14 as a neuroimmune regulator in autoinflammatory pediatric fever disorders.
summary_ja: 家族性地中海熱（FMF）およびPFAPA症候群の小児患者46名および48名と、健常対照群46名を対象に、血清フェニキシン-14（PNX-14）濃度を評価する横断研究が行われた。発作期のPNX-14濃度は、非発作期および健常対照群と比較して有意に高い値を示した。また、PNX-14濃度はCRPと中等度の正の相関を示したが、ESRや病勢度スコア、コルヒチン治療とは有意な関連が認められなかった。PNX-14は自己炎症過程における炎症消退を目指す神経免疫応答の一部である可能性が示唆された。
summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated serum phoenixin-14 (PNX-14) levels in 140 children, including those with FMF, PFAPA, and healthy controls. Serum PNX-14 levels were significantly elevated during attack periods compared to attack-free periods and healthy controls, showing a moderate positive correlation with CRP. The findings suggest PNX-14 may participate in a neuroimmune response involved in resolving inflammation during autoinflammatory attacks.
key_finding_ja: FMFおよびPFAPA患者の発作期において血清PNX-14濃度が有意に上昇しており、CRPと正の相関を示すことが明らかになった。
why_it_matters_ja: PNX-14が自己炎症性疾患における炎症制御に関与する神経ペプチドバイオマーカーとして機能する可能性が期待される。

title: Neurodegeneration as an early driver and therapeutic target in diabetic retinopathy.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is conventionally recognized as a microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus. Nevertheless, accumulating evidence confirms that early retinal neurodegeneration develops in the course of diabetes and drives early visual impairment. Multiple studies have verified that abnormal retinal neural responses frequently emerge before identifiable microvascular lesions. This review therefore systematically summarizes existing evidence confirming retinal neurodegeneration as a core, early pathological event in diabetic retinal disease (DRD), elaborates the cellular and metabolic mechanisms of neurodegeneration inside the retinal neurovascular unit (NVU), and assesses novel neuroprotective therapeutic modalities. Retinal neurodegeneration manifests prior to clinically apparent microvascular complications. NVU dysfunction, triggered by neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, advanced glycation end products (AGEs), excitotoxicity and mitochondrial dysfunction, serves as the pivotal pathway mediating neuronal injury. Notably, current vasculotropic therapies fail to effectively block early neuronal dysfunction. By comparison, neuroprotective interventions targeting oxidative stress, inflammatory cascades, glial dysfunction, deficient neurotrophic supply and mitochondrial damage exhibit promising effects on maintaining retinal neuronal architecture and function. In conclusion, retinal neurodegeneration constitutes a core pathological cascade of DR. Incorporating neuroprotective regimens into established treatment systems facilitates earlier intervention, optimizes visual function prognosis, and ultimately transforms the clinical management paradigm of DRD toward retinal neural protection.
authors: Wang CN, Xia YH, Huang H, Xu YX, Zhao DM, Dong JL, Ye HJ.
screening_reason: Focuses on retinal neurodegeneration driven by neuroinflammation and cellular stress in diabetic retinopathy.
summary_ja: 糖尿病網膜症（DR）における網膜神経変性が、微小血管病変に先行して生じる初期の核心的病理プロセスであることをまとめたレビューである。網膜神経血管ユニットの機能障害は、神経炎症、酸化ストレス、興奮毒性、ミトコンドリア障害などによって引き起こされる。酸化ストレスや炎症カスケード、グリア細胞障害を標的とした神経保護療法が、網膜神経の構造と機能を維持する新たな治療選択肢として注目されている。
summary_en: This review establishes retinal neurodegeneration as an early driver of visual dysfunction in diabetic retinopathy, occurring prior to clinically evident microvascular lesions. Neurovascular unit dysfunction is mediated by neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, advanced glycation end products, and mitochondrial impairment. Neuroprotective interventions targeting these pathways show promise in preserving retinal neural architecture and modifying current treatment paradigms.
key_finding_ja: 糖尿病網膜症において網膜神経変性は微小血管障害に先行する早期病変であり、神経炎症や酸化ストレスを標的とした神経保護療法の重要性が示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 従来の血管選択的治療に加え、神経保護アプローチを導入することで糖尿病網膜症の早期介入および予後改善に繋がる可能性がある。

title: Schisandrin A, a dietary lignan from Schisandra chinensis, ameliorates cognitive deficits in AlCl₃/D-galactose-treated mice.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with limited disease-modifying therapies. Chronic aluminum exposure, a well-recognized environmental risk factor, exacerbates AD pathogenesis by driving oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Schisandrin A (SchA), a bioactive lignan from the medicinal and edible plant Schisandra chinensis, exhibits promising antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, yet its nutritional relevance for AD intervention remains undefined. This study evaluated SchA's neuroprotective potential in an AlCl₃/D-galactose-induced cognitive impairment model. We found that SchA significantly ameliorated learning and memory impairments in Morris water maze, novel object recognition, open field and Y-maze tests, alleviated neuronal damage in the hippocampus and cortex, and reduced cerebral amyloid-β (Aβ) production in AlCl₃/D-galactose-treated mice. Mechanistically, SchA mitigated neuroinflammation via inhibiting the IKK/NF-κB/iNOS pathway, and alleviated oxidative stress through activating the Nrf2/HO-1 axis. Our findings demonstrate that SchA exerts neuroprotective effects in AlCl₃/D-galactose-treated mice, accompanied by modulation of inflammatory and oxidative-stress-related signalling, supporting its potential as a nutritional intervention for AD.
authors: Xue JS, Niu M, Song XY, Deng XM.
screening_reason: Evaluates attenuation of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress by Schisandrin A in a mouse model of cognitive impairment.
summary_ja: 本研究では、塩化アルミニウムおよびD-ガラクトースにより誘導した認知機能障害マウスモデルを用いて、五味子由来の木質素化合物シザンドリンA（SchA）の神経保護効果を検証した。SchAの投与により、学習・記憶障害が有意に改善し、海馬および大脳皮質における神経細胞損傷とアミロイドβの産生が軽減した。作用機序として、SchAはIKK/NF-κB/iNOS経路を抑制することで神経炎症を抑え、Nrf2/HO-1軸を活性化することで酸化ストレスを緩和することが示された。これらの結果は、SchAが認知症に対する栄養学的介入の候補となり得ることを示している。
summary_en: This study evaluated the neuroprotective effects of Schisandrin A (SchA), a dietary lignan from Schisandra chinensis, in an AlCl3/D-galactose-induced mouse model of cognitive impairment. Treatment with SchA significantly improved learning and memory deficits, reduced hippocampal and cortical neuronal damage, and decreased cerebral amyloid-β production. Mechanistically, SchA attenuated neuroinflammation by inhibiting the IKK/NF-κB/iNOS pathway and reduced oxidative stress through activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 axis.
key_finding_ja: シザンドリンAは、IKK/NF-κB/iNOS経路の抑制とNrf2/HO-1軸の活性化を介して、モデルマウスの神経炎症と酸化ストレスを緩和し、認知機能を改善した。
why_it_matters_ja: 食事由来成分による神経炎症および酸化ストレスの制御可能性が示されたことで、アルツハイマー病に対する予防・介入アプローチの開発につながる可能性がある。

title: Management of Musculoskeletal Injuries with an Inflammatory Damage-Associated Molecular Pattern (DAMP) Etiology.
abstract: Introduction Musculoskeletal injuries (MSKI) often progress from acute tissue damage to chronic pain and dysfunction when mechanical overload and microdamage sustain sterile inflammation and neuroimmune sensitization. These processes amplify nociception, impair loading tolerance, and limit the efficacy of rehabilitation, underscoring the need for mechanism-based strategies that interrupt the transition from acute injury to chronic musculoskeletal disease. Methods This etiological review was conducted in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar (1990-2026) identified mechanistic, translational, and therapeutic research reports that examined damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) signaling, innate immune activation, stromal cell responses, nociceptor sensitization, and interventions targeting these pathways. Eligible studies addressed DAMP-related mechanisms in musculoskeletal tissues or evaluated therapies that modulate the underlying inflammatory and mechanobiological drivers of chronic MSKI. Information was synthesized thematically to construct an integrated model of how DAMPs contribute to chronicity. Results Across tendon, cartilage, ligament, muscle, and fibrocartilage, mechanical overload and microdamage trigger the release of DAMPs that activate Toll-like receptors (TLRs), receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE), and inflammasome pathways, thereby sustaining cytokine production, stromal cell activation, and nociceptor sensitization. Persistent DAMP signaling is strongly associated with impaired inflammation resolution, failed tissue healing, and progression to chronic tendinopathy, osteoarthritis, and mechanical low back pain. Emerging therapeutic approaches, including targeted loading, regenerative injections, metabolic modulation, and immune-modifying strategies, demonstrate potential to attenuate DAMP activity, promote resolution, and restore tissue homeostasis. Conclusions Sterile inflammation driven by DAMPs provides a unifying mechanistic framework explaining why many musculoskeletal injuries fail to resolve and instead evolve into chronic, refractory conditions. Therapies that modulate DAMP signaling, enhance inflammatory resolution, and normalize mechanobiological loading represent promising avenues for preventing or reversing chronic MSKI pathology. A mechanistically informed approach may improve clinical outcomes by addressing the etiological drivers rather than the downstream symptoms of chronic musculoskeletal disease.
authors: Love RJ, Sheridan J, Funk C, Young JL.
screening_reason: Reviews DAMP-driven neuroimmune sensitization, sterile inflammation, and nociceptor activation in chronic musculoskeletal injury.
summary_ja: 筋骨格系損傷（MSKI）における機械的過負荷および微細損傷が、ダメージ関連分子パターン（DAMPs）を介して無菌的炎症と神経免疫感作を引き起こすメカニズムを解説したレビューである。DAMPsはTLRやRAGEなどの受容体を刺激し、持続的なサイトカイン産生と痛覚受容体の感作を誘発する。DAMPsシグナルの抑制や炎症消退の促進を目指した治療アプローチが、慢性痛への移行を防ぐ新たな戦略として期待されている。
summary_en: This narrative review highlights how mechanical overload in musculoskeletal injuries triggers the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), driving sterile inflammation and neuroimmune sensitization. DAMP signaling via TLR and RAGE pathways leads to sustained cytokine production and nociceptor sensitization, contributing to chronic tendinopathy and back pain. Modulating DAMP pathways and enhancing inflammatory resolution present potential therapeutic avenues to restore tissue homeostasis.
key_finding_ja: 筋骨格系損傷におけるDAMPs主導の無菌的炎症と神経免疫感作が、慢性痛や組織修復不全への移行に関与していることが明示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 慢性筋骨格系疾患の病態解明に基づき、症状緩和にとどまらない根本的治療戦略の確立に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Leukocyte telomere length and gut microbiome profiles in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and at-risk conditions.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, highlighting the need for minimally invasive biomarkers capable of distinguishing it from related risk conditions. This study evaluated relative leukocyte telomere length (LTL) and gut microbiome profiles as potential biomarkers for PDAC. The study included 244 participants with PDAC (n = 37), chronic pancreatitis (CP; n = 56), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM; n = 99), or no related risk conditions (controls; n = 52). LTL was measured by monochrome multiplex quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), while gut microbiome composition was assessed by 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing in a subset of participants with PDAC (n = 12), CP (n = 13), and controls (n = 7). LTL varied with age, sex, and smoking status. After adjustment for these factors, patients with PDAC had significantly longer LTL than controls (p = 0.029), whereas differences between PDAC and CP or T2DM were not significant. LTL showed limited ability to discriminate PDAC from controls (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.651) and was not associated with overall survival. Gut microbiome diversity and taxonomic composition did not differ significantly among the analyzed groups. These findings indicate that LTL has limited utility as a standalone diagnostic or prognostic biomarker for PDAC but may warrant further evaluation as a complementary marker in larger prospective studies. The exploratory microbiome findings also require validation in adequately powered cohorts.
authors: Kharazishvili K, Hujova A, Hucl T, Balounova K, Vokacova K, Kroupa M.
screening_reason: Evaluates gut microbiome composition and diversity alongside telomere length as potential biomarkers for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
summary_ja: 膵管腺がん（PDAC）の低侵襲バイオマーカーとして、白血球テロメア長（LTL）および腸内細菌叢の有用性を244名の参加者を対象に評価した。年齢や喫煙状況などの調整後、PDAC患者は対照群と比較して有意に長いLTLを示したが、識別能は限定的であった。また、PDAC、慢性膵炎、対照群の間で腸内細菌叢の多様性や分類組成に有意な差は認められなかった。
summary_en: This study evaluated relative leukocyte telomere length (LTL) and gut microbiome profiles as potential biomarkers for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) across 244 participants. Although PDAC patients exhibited significantly longer LTL compared to controls after adjusting for covariates, LTL showed limited diagnostic accuracy and no survival association. Gut microbiome diversity and composition did not significantly differ between PDAC, chronic pancreatitis, and control groups.
key_finding_ja: 白血球テロメア長および腸内細菌叢プロファイルは、単独のPDAC診断バイオマーカーとしては限定的な有用性しか示さなかった。
why_it_matters_ja: PDAC早期診断のためのバイオマーカー開発において、単独指標の限界を示すとともに、大規模コホートでの検証の必要性を示している。

title: Effects of Micro- and Nanoplastic Exposure During Critical Developmental Periods on the Central Nervous System: A Systematic Review of Rodent Models.
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are persistent environmental pollutants capable of crossing biological barriers, including the placenta and the blood-brain barrier, raising concerns about their impact on neurodevelopment. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from experimental rodent models, revealing morphological, molecular, and behavioral alterations associated with developmental MNPs exposure in rodent models and highlighting their potential relevance for understanding neurodevelopmental vulnerability. Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO CRD420251127469), MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched without date limits (last search: 18 Aug 2025). The review followed a PECO framework: population: mammalian in vivo models; exposure: MNPs during gestation, lactation, childhood, or adolescence; comparator: non-exposed or vehicle-treated controls; outcomes: behavioral, structural, or molecular central nervous system effects. Study reliability was assessed using ToxRTool. Due to heterogeneity, findings were narratively synthesized by exposure window (prenatal, postnatal, combined prenatal-early postnatal exposure). Of 542 records, 20 studies met inclusion criteria. All included studies used rodents (mice or rats) and evaluated polystyrene, polypropylene, polyethylene, or polyvinyl chloride particles delivered mainly by oral routes. Our analysis identified the central nervous system as an important target of MNPs, with convergent findings across exposure windows revealing oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation (microglial/astrocytic activation), apoptosis/ferroptosis, disrupted neurogenesis and myelination, and synaptic/dendritic abnormalities. Neurochemical alterations frequently involved GABAergic and glutamatergic imbalance, with context-specific dopaminergic changes. Behaviorally, MNPs were associated with impaired learning and memory, increased anxiety-like responses, altered sociability, and repetitive/stereotyped behaviors. Several studies suggested microbiota-gut-brain interactions via intestinal barrier disruption, dysbiosis, and systemic inflammation. In rodent models, the available evidence suggests that early-life MNPs exposure may contribute to developmental neurotoxicity, which is characterized by multilevel central nervous system alterations and behavioral impairments. Standardized, environmentally relevant exposure paradigms, sex-stratified analyses, and longitudinal follow-up are needed to clarify dose-response, persistence, and human relevance.
authors: Gomes CB, Cruz TA, Kraisch RJ, Brocardo PS, Farina M, Marzola P.
screening_reason: Systematic review focusing on developmental neurotoxicity including central neuroinflammation and gut-brain interactions triggered by micro/nanoplastic exposure.
summary_ja: 発達期におけるマイクロ・ナノプラスチック（MNP）曝露が中央神経系に及ぼす影響について、齧歯類モデルを用いた20件の研究を体系的にレビューした。MNP曝露はミクログリアやアストロサイトの活性化といった神経炎症、酸化ストレス、神経伝達物質の不均衡を引き起こすことが報告されている。また、学習・記憶障害や不安様行動などの行動異常、腸管バリア機能の破綻を通じた腸・脳相関の変容も示唆されている。
summary_en: This systematic review analyzed 20 rodent studies evaluating the impact of early-life exposure to micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) on the central nervous system. Early MNP exposure induced neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, neurotransmitter imbalances, and behavioral impairments such as cognitive deficits and anxiety-like behaviors. The findings also highlighted potential gut-brain axis involvement through intestinal barrier disruption and dysbiosis.
key_finding_ja: 発達期のマイクロ・ナノプラスチック曝露は、齧歯類モデルにおいて神経炎症や酸化ストレス、神経伝達物質の失調に伴う行動異常を誘発することが示された。
why_it_matters_ja: 環境汚染物質による脳発達へのリスク理解を深める重要な知見であるが、人間への外挿や標準化された曝露条件での評価が今後の課題である。

title: Severe Burn Injury as a Chronic Immunometabolic Disease.
abstract: Over the past five decades, advances in acute burn care have markedly improved early survival following severe thermal injury. However, long-term epidemiologic studies demonstrate that burn survivors remain at increased risk for metabolic disease, cardiovascular pathology, malignancy, cognitive impairment, and accelerated aging, well beyond wound closure. These observations suggest that severe burn injury can initiate a chronic disease state characterized by persistent physiologic dysregulation in a subset of patients. Emerging evidence indicates that this phenotype is driven by sustained immunometabolic dysfunction, in which immune and metabolic pathways are tightly coupled and mutually reinforcing. Severe burn injury induces durable reprogramming of innate and adaptive immune cells alongside prolonged hypermetabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroendocrine stress signaling. This results in a persistent inflammatory, immunosuppressed, catabolic syndrome (PIICS), where chronic inflammation coexists with impaired adaptive immunity and ongoing amino acid depletion. In this review, we synthesize population-based, clinical, and experimental data supporting burn injury as a chronic immunometabolic disease. We highlight key mechanisms linking immune dysfunction with altered substrate utilization, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and neuroimmune signaling, and discuss how these pathways contribute to long-term organ dysfunction. Finally, we outline emerging opportunities for risk stratification and therapeutic interventions targeting integrated immunometabolic pathways.
authors: Vogler TO, Dyamenahalli KU, Mueller SW, Wiktor AJ, McMahan RH, Halevi AE, Kovacs EJ.
screening_reason: Reviews systemic immunometabolic and neuroimmune signaling dysregulation following severe burn injury.
summary_ja: 本レビューは、重症熱傷が急性期を越えて持続的な免疫代謝機能障害を引き起こし、慢性疾患状態へと進行するメカニズムを概括している。重症熱傷後には、自然免疫および獲得免疫細胞の永続的な再プログラミング、持続的な過代謝、ミトコンドリア機能障害、神経内分泌ストレスシグナルが生じる。これにより、慢性炎症と適応免疫低下、アミノ酸枯渇が共存する持続性炎症・免疫抑制・異化症候群（PIICS）が誘発される。著者らは、免疫障害と基質利用、ミトコンドリア生体エネルギー学、神経免疫シグナルとの関連性を整理し、長期的な器官障害への関与を論じている。
summary_en: This review synthesizes clinical and experimental evidence establishing severe burn injury as a chronic immunometabolic disease extending beyond acute wound closure. Severe burns induce long-lasting reprogramming of immune cells, prolonged hypermetabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroendocrine stress signaling, leading to a persistent inflammatory, immunosuppressed, catabolic syndrome (PIICS). The authors highlight the molecular links between immune dysregulation and metabolic alteration, discussing potential therapeutic targets to prevent long-term organ dysfunction.
key_finding_ja: 重症熱傷は持続的な免疫代謝機能障害や神経免疫シグナルの異常を引き起こし、創傷治癒後も続く慢性疾患状態を形成する。
why_it_matters_ja: 熱傷生存者における長期的な器官障害や代謝異常の背景メカニズムが解明されることで、急性期以降の新たなリスク分類や標的治療法の開発に寄与する可能性がある。

title: Correction: circ_0044235 exacerbates neuroinflammation and apoptosis following spinal cord injury by targeting miR-338-5p.
authors: Lin M, Huang L, Zhang B, Wang Y, Zhu X, Zeng W.
journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
screening_reason: This erratum notice pertains directly to a primary study examining circ_0044235 in regulating neuroinflammation following spinal cord injury.
summary_ja: 本論文は、脊髄損傷後の神経炎症とアポトーシスにおけるcirc_0044235とmiR-338-5pの役割を扱った既報論文に対する訂正（Correction）記事である。提供された抄録本文には特定のデータや結果の記述は含まれていない。研究の正確な内容や修正箇所については元の原著論文を参照する必要がある。
summary_en: This is a correction notice for a previously published study concerning the role of circ_0044235 and miR-338-5p in neuroinflammation and apoptosis following spinal cord injury. No abstract text or specific study data are provided in this notice. Readers should consult the original publication for detailed methodological and experimental findings.
key_finding_ja: 本文献は脊髄損傷後の神経炎症に関連する論文の訂正通知である。
why_it_matters_ja: 学術論文の正確性を担保し誤解を防ぐために訂正情報の確認は重要である。
